## The infinite regress 🔒

The split is **beginningless and infinite.** The One fragments into ever-smaller pieces; a piece that comes apart far enough becomes a new level (see the Law below, which replaces the older spatial phrasing). Any "origin" we can name is only the ceiling of our perception, not of reality. Fractal — the same scattering at every level, up and down. [REV v5-cc] (Understood as a regress of **consciousness** scattering, layered on the pre-existing physical universe; **between planes the nesting is also by scale and is simply real** — "were only 1 tiny particle in something much larger all the way up"; "every iota… self-contained universes themselves all the way down"; "Its one of those things we just have to say is real. Thats part of the magic" (BANK 11-02; cc R101). Universes are still not *born from physics*, and nothing here is explained or audited.) (was: "(Understood as a regress of **consciousness** scattering, layered on the pre-existing physical universe — NOT a regress of universes being born from physics.)")

## THE LAW OF THE REGRESS 🔒 (t166, t168, t170, t172 — Patrick-stated)
> *"all the way up the same story is playing... each stage is a being decohering so far it becomes an entirely new plane of reality and theres always the part who is clinging together still."* — Patrick (t172)

- **Every plane is a being that came apart.** A being decoheres into many; when it decoheres far enough, it **can no longer pull itself back together** — it has forgotten it was once something more (t164, t166). *(Codex label for that point of no return: the **forgetting horizon** — Claude's term, t167, for Patrick's "go too far... and they can never remember who they were to return.")* What has dissolved past that point **becomes the plane below**.
- **There is always a part that clings.** Beside every coming-apart, some part holds itself together and refuses to dissolve (t172).
- **The One is exactly this:** *"He decohered into everything and now he cant pull back together. This is what happens on the infinite regress. A new smaller being who forgot it was once something more decoheres again to split itself into pieces over and over."* — Patrick (t166). This is why the One cannot come home (canon never said why before).
- **Our level (t168, t170):** one level up, a single being came apart. The pieces that **let go entirely** became Ones — ours became our level. The pieces that **held on** are the **Unified Ones**. **The One and the Unified Ones are siblings** from the same source.
- ✅ **GUARD-RAIL — shared law, not shared lineage (t167):** *(verify fix: was 🔒. The guard-rail is Claude's and Patrick did not object; the lineage half is already locked under* In-betweeners *below.)* the in-betweeners' coherence-splitting (`06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`) is *the same law of selves* the One obeys — **not** shared ancestry. In-betweeners remain a separate lineage (see below). Do not reopen the lineage question.
- **Nobody resets the regress (t239 — Claude's wording correction, accepted by silence; not locked):** *(r2 fix: was stamped 🔒; the ledger marks this "confirmed softly".)* the regress is the cosmic law, not something anyone can undo. What Derrek holds together is **this world, against the door he opened** — not the regress.
- Physics stays flavor: "decoherence" is borrowed vocabulary, not a mechanism to audit.

The others are the **parallel / sister worlds** — **siblings from the same source, not copies** (t191). Every world is the only one of its kind; resemblances between them are family resemblance, not clones.

## The DEAD UNIVERSE & the planet-roster cap ⚖️
The physical cosmos is **real but eerily LIFELESS beyond Earth** — the planets are all out there, but the universe is dead. **The One "chose" Earth** for unspecified reasons (background, held loosely — does NOT need to be airtight; "the One chose this world" is enough). This **caps the authoring burden permanently:** other worlds are lifeless rocks the races later settle — **no native populaces to invent, ever.** When the far-future species branch into space, they find it all weirdly dead and colonize empty worlds (`07_BEINGS.md` far-future). Alien *life* effectively none; alien *minds* none. *(This concerns our universe. Sibling worlds are separate universes with their own Ones — above.)* [NEW v5-wk] Earth is everyone's homeworld (wk W58); all gods are born of flesh, on one world (wk W30).
- 🌊 **TBD candidate thread (not locked):** some catastrophic event in the deep past drove all life to converge on the one safe world (Earth) and colonize it together — recasting Earth as "the place life *fled to*." A good far-future mystery hook (why is everything dead?), pairs with the end-of-time register. Develop or discard later.

🚫 **RETIRED — the portal-bootstrap keystone (explored & SCRAPPED):** the idea that Jon & Derrek built the portal in a magicless far-future, which fused the One *into* our universe, made Earth the convergence point, and explained why the elder races "woke up"/spawned in. **Scrapped** because it created an eating-its-tail paradox (the One can't be all-consciousness without the portal; they couldn't build the portal without consciousness; and Jon/Derrek were conscious *before* it). Reverted to the standing cosmology: the One is the beginningless, background origin of consciousness; the portal is just a thing Jon & Derrek built, NOT the origin of magic or the universe. (The elder races' "awakening" stays as established — they simply *were*, the day the world was blessed — `07_BEINGS.md`; not a portal-spawn.) **v5 (t182–184):** Patrick's "they forced their earth to become this world" was reconciled without reviving the keystone — *"They didnt create the one but their portal opened the protective shield the unified one had established"* (see *The Breach*). The keystone stays retired.

🚫 **RETIRED OUTRIGHT — Reunion↔Separation & cosmic Light/Dark (scrapped):** the two poles/impulses; the Light as a cosmic being ("son of the One," guardian, gatherer); the Dark as the named scattered remainder; the one-way fall & the gathering; pole-positions as character features; motivation-by-pole ("kills to reunite Remnant" — exactly the cookie-cutter formula we refuse). **Light and dark return to being VARIABLES** — free descriptors (morality, aesthetics, expression-flavor) with no cosmic doctrine. The old naming collision with morality-light/dark is moot: there is no cosmic Light/Dark to collide with. *(v5: the Law of the Regress's clinging/dissolving and the pull of reunion are not these poles returning — they give no character a pole-position or a pole-motive. ⚠️ Boundary flagged for Patrick.)*

## Unified Ones & the Blight — REDEFINED 🔒 (t174, t176, t178)
> *"Its literally a being dissolving itself into more beings and the blight is the name for those who wish to exploit and destroy those smaller; unified ones are the ones who wish to protect the shatter."* — Patrick (t174)
> *"Unified one is those who as the name suggests hold together and the blight is the name for the parts who seek maximum dissolution."* — Patrick (t176)

- **The Unified Ones** = those who **hold together** — the pieces that clung when the being above came apart (t168, t176); siblings of the One. They **wish to protect the shatter** (t174). They created the **BUBBLE/barrier** that holds the Blight out, keeping our level safe (standing canon; t184: "the protective shield the unified one had established"). ## In-betweeners — a separate ancient lineage 🔒

(See `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`.)

[NEW v5-wk] **They stay alien and separate; they are the Qu-like remakers** (wk W37). ## Death & the soul 🔒 (consciousness side)

A fragment's natural post-death process is its own. The deepest violations — now understood as **soul magic** (the rare branch: Spirit gripping another fragment rather than matter — `04_MAGIC_SUBSTRATE.md`):
- **Soul binding** — forcibly interrupting that process (violating the One's self-determination). *(v5 — t504–513: binding is **concentration** — the holder pays, constantly; kill the holder and the bound soul is [REV v5-cc] freed, its Remnant released (cc R096) (was: "freed or destroyed"); the vessel varies. Mechanics in `04_MAGIC_SUBSTRATE.md`.)*
- **Soul harvesting** — absorbing another's fragment into your living one: gain power *and* their dominant tendency fighting yours → increasingly plural/fractured. [REV v5-cc] One way to hold more Remnant than your own, beside devices and grafted flesh (cc R097) (was: "The only way to raise innate Remnant"), and it fragments you. (The self-risk that limits all soul magic, in its most extreme form.) [NEW v5-wk] Taking others' Remnant is **"stealing their production"**: [REV v5-wk2] [REV v5-cc] the mechanism is an amplifier — "I think its an amplifier only" (BANK 10-31); "drives their grip" retires (cc R132) (was: "the mechanism is 🌊 open — the thief driving their grip, or 'using an amplifier to touch a wider pool' (Patrick, chat t83: 'Im not sure')") (was: "the thief drives their grip" — Claude's t84 framing, never confirmed) (wk W11). Changelings take 1–2 souls at a time (wk W16).
- **Harvest into a working — Convergence** (t43, t54; banked t103): [REV v5-wk] **Convergence works on bodies.** The funerary version **releases** the soul; the emperor's version **trapped the city's Remnant in the stone** — he was a mix of souls and dissolved, too many at once (wk W15). Remnant cannot be burned or spent (wk W10). **The original Convergence was god-forging**; its lost secret was silencing the crowd into unison — **"soul mortar"**; the greatest giant god is a million minds in unison (wk W17). (was: "harvested Remnant burned as fuel for a will-imposed transmutation, 'when soul and matter become one.'") Detail in `07_BEINGS.md`.
- [REV v5-cc] **Enchantment is simply Remnant held inside something, in many uses and forms** (cc R099). (was: "[NEW v5-wk] **Enchantment = a soul held in matter** (wk W12)" as the whole rule.) A bound soul feels [REV v5-cc] only vague, general things, maybe some strangeness — "sensation comes from sensory organs" (BANK 11-02); dread is flavor, not the rule (cc R128) (was: "dread, without a brain to understand it") (wk W13). Objects hold souls without a holder's concentration; ghosts need a holder (wk W14) [REV v5-wk2: 🌊 proposed, unconfirmed — Claude's proposal (chat t82); Patrick moved on and never addressed it]. Mechanics: `04_MAGIC_SUBSTRATE.md`, `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`.
- **Echoes, ghosts, changelings are three different things (t498–501):** an **echo** is loose Remnant left by great death — impressions, no one there — that fades over time; a **ghost** is *"remnant which was bound together by magic"* (Patrick, t500), so every true ghost is a soul-binding crime; a **changeling** is many souls bound into one living driver. Mechanics in `04_MAGIC_SUBSTRATE.md`.
- [NEW v5-jul] **Body theft** ✅ — soul magic can override another being's Remnant and take the body over: *"how else would another human use soul magic to invade and take their body over without that implicit ability in our system to override someone's remnant and steal their body"* (Patrick, jul08 t329). This is the "move body" door to becoming a changeling (phys t676). (Claude's name "domination" for this outcome was never confirmed.)
- [NEW v5-jul] **The brain is not the fragment** ✅ (jul08 t331–332, t341–343): the fragment is the presence and identity; the brain is the physical organ a present fragment thinks through. A body in a vegetative state has not lost its Remnant — *"just that their brain isnt functioning"* (Patrick, t331). The fragment leaves at **death as an event**, not at the loss of an organ (Claude t342, accepted t343: *"the beautifully grimdark interpretation"*); so a person whose brain is destroyed or replaced while the body lives stays inside, *"locked inside as a vague state. They feel whats happening tho with no brain they cannot actually interpret the signals"* — the same dread as a soul trapped in an artifact (Patrick, t341). (The character built on this, the ASI in a human body, is story material and was left unruled at phys t629–630 — `07`/`09`.)

An elf who dies far away **dies alone, without the bond** (wk W08). ## What magic IS 🔒

- **REMNANT = the chunk of the One that you ARE.** Your fragment of consciousness; your capacity — how much of reality you can grip at once. [REV v5-cc] Innate, and **capped by the body's physical capacity**; devices and grafted flesh add capacity that holds more, and soul magic crams more in, held by Will and your own Remnant's coherence (cc R097). (was: "Innate, fixed in the living, raisable only by harvesting (which fragments you).") It is **identity, not fuel** — you can touch the world *because you are a remnant of the One*. Not mana, not a pool, not spent per cast. [NEW v5-wk] **Remnant cannot be burned or spent** — "we cant burn remnant" (wk W10). Soul = Remnant (wk W07).
  - [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **What Remnant measures:** "It is a measure of how much of the one is held together" (Patrick, BANK 11-16) (cc R021).
  - [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **The body holds it.** A body has the structures to hold its Remnant; "any strong user likely has a body naturally capable of holding the amount of remnant they can control." Giants, the largest living bodies, have the most capacity (Patrick, BANK 11-16) (cc R023).
- **REMNANT IS AGELESS.** (t678 — Patrick: "I think remnant is ageless.") The fragment of the One does not age; **flesh does.** More Remnant makes the flesh resist age more strongly (Law 4a) — resistance, never immunity. *(This retires the old changeling "founder's clock" aging line — that line lives in `07_BEINGS.md`; see routing.)*
- **SPIRIT = the name for active Remnant magic** — a being's faculty for **consciously manipulating matter** (and, rarely, other consciousness). Spirit is *the system itself*: having it is what distinguishes a conscious being from inert flesh. **Flesh is just flesh; Spirit is what reaches out and acts.** (This replaces the old "Spirit = the consciousness-half of a two-part system." There is no two-part system anymore. Spirit = using your Remnant. Full stop.)
- **MAGIC = inherited mastery, science-flavored.** The One mastered the universe (wielder-in-chief, not author); a being's magic is a lesser expression of that same mastery — a fragment doing what the One does. [REV v5-wk] **The grip is now mechanized; the sense stays mysterious** (wk W06) — see *The appendage and the inner sense* below. (was: "There is **no interface mechanism** to explain; the capacity is identity ('how?' bottoms out at 'you are a piece of the One').") In-world, **"magic" and "science" are the same word** — people do not distinguish them; what we call physics they call the workings of magic. [NEW v5-wk] Humans call magic "science" because dragons were humanity's first teachers (wk W63); faith, magic and science are one act under different names (wk W57).
- [NEW v5-wk] **THE APPENDAGE — the grip, mechanized.** Remnant extends an **appendage** that grabs the universe. Its length, size, shape and intensity scale with Remnant, skill and focus (wk W01). What the grip does (flavor-level, no math): shaking particles = heat; pulling charges apart = lightning; crushing or ripping the nucleus = explosions; turning a quark = transmutation — **the hardest act**; a botched transmutation rips the nucleus; denting space = gravity (wk W02). Dragons stay four-legged; the appendage is their hands (wk W63).
- [REV v5-cc] **Sensing is part of Skill, not a dial** (cc R095): the perception text below is kept as the sense-and-touch side of Skill. (was the heading: "THE INNER SENSE — unexplained.") [NEW v5-wk] An unexplained perception that comes from Remnant, **separate from the appendage**, both trainable and innate (wk W03). Patrick: "you mostly feel with a second inner sense." "Feel" returns as skill — a dial, not a gate (wk W05). It stays mysterious (wk W06). **Sensing other beings' Remnant is a rare master-level skill** — "Some very talented masters have learned to sense other beings remnant. This is rare" (wk W07). [REV v5-cc] ✅ **Sensing scales with the source** (Law 3): "If your a powerful user you can sense remnant and magic in general… youd feel the tower like the sun"; "those mildly psychicly aware would feel ghosts" (BANK 11-16). A huge source is felt by many; one being's Remnant only by rare masters (cc R129). (was: rarity read as covering every source.) On the page soul-sensing must be **rare, felt rather than reported, and unreliable** — never "video gamey," no constant scanning or detecting (wk W09).
- **One undivided act.** A being reaches out with Spirit and makes reality do what they want. That's the whole of it. What the act *looks like* (fire, gravity, a shove, a transmutation) is description applied afterward, never a separate kind of magic.
- **Rifts are reservoirs, never the source.** (t186–188.) The rifts leak power from the level above and are large reservoirs of magic that people fight over — but they are **not the source of magic.** Every being's magic is still its own soul. (Cosmology of the rifts: `03_COSMOLOGY.md`.)
  - [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **Loose Remnant and wells.** "Remnant is just randomly floating around"; it gathers in latent pools that are found and mined "like oil reserves." Rift sites are the richest (Patrick, BANK 11-02, ruling sets 1–2) (cc R025).
- [NEW v5-jul] **REMNANT IS NOT TRANSFERABLE.** Patrick (jul23 t108): "remnant isn't transferable. They cant give their remnant they only give the knowledge or ability to use it." (jul23 t114): "Remnant is no longer transferable." No being can give, lend, or slowly siphon its Remnant to another — what passes between beings is knowledge or technique, never capacity (the pact rework, approved t630; `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`). [REV v5-cc] **Reconciled with the capacity cap (cc R097):** your own fragment can't be given away, but extra Remnant can be **held** in added capacity (devices, grafted flesh) or crammed in by soul magic. (was: wholesale absorption as the only way to hold more.) **Wholesale absorption is the one exception** — slow siphoning is retired, but full possession/absorption is not (jul23 t116; see *Wholesale absorption* under Soul magic). [REV v5-wk] *Settled against them: Remnant cannot be burned or spent (wk W10), so rift Remnant drawn into a body and burned (t768) and stolen souls spent in an attack (t342, t774) are overturned as mechanics; their home files (`05`, `08`, `09`) must revise the scenes.* (was: "🌊 *Rift Remnant drawn into a body (t768) and stolen souls spent in an attack (t342, t774) sit uneasily beside this — flagged, not settled here (changes files).*")
- [NEW v5-wk] **STEALING PRODUCTION.** Taking others' Remnant = "stealing their production": **[REV v5-wk2] [REV v5-cc] the mechanism is an amplifier — "I think its an amplifier only" (BANK 10-31); "drives their grip" retires (cc R132) (was: "the mechanism is 🌊 open — the thief driving their grip, or 'using an amplifier to touch a wider pool' (Patrick, chat t83: 'Im not sure')") (was: "the thief drives their grip" — Claude's t84 framing, never confirmed)** (wk W11). Derrek's orc chips are this (wk W51).

## REMNANT, WILL, SKILL = POWER — the only gates 🔒
[REV v5-cc] (heading, cc R095; was: "REMNANT + SKILL = POWER — the only gates 🔒")

[REV v5-cc] **Three independent dials — Remnant (how much), Will (force of will), and Skill (how well, including sense and touch)** — plus the bill, effort/fatigue, and burnout past it (cc R095, R096). (was: "[REV v5-wk] **Three independent dials — Remnant (strength), control (skill), and the inner sense** (wk W03) — plus the bill, effort/fatigue." Earlier: "The entire mechanical statement of a being, and the **only** limits on magic:") The limits on magic:
- **REMNANT (how much)** — capacity; how much reality you can grip at once. [REV v5-cc] Innate, capped by physical capacity; added capacity (devices, grafted flesh) and soul magic can hold more (cc R097). (was: "Innate, fixed.") More Remnant = more possible power (you can't grip more than you have consciousness to grip with). This is the natural ceiling.
- **SKILL / MASTERY (how well)** — how finely you grip, shape, and **blend**. Learned; grows with training and time. Combinatorial fluency. Distinct from raw Remnant; two beings of equal Remnant produce utterly different results. [NEW v5-wk] The rulings call this dial **control** (wk W03). [REV v5-cc] **Skill is your training and covers sense and touch** — "The skill is like your training. How many times have yiu sat down and tried to find the nucleus of an atom" (cc R095). (was: Skill as control only.)
- [NEW v5-cc] **WILL (how much you mean it)** — force of will: conviction, moral weight, wanting it. "How confident are you. How much do you really want this. Its like force of will" (cc R095). A timid giant can't force his fire to obey; a trained, willful gnome still can't quite beat a dragon (BANK 11-16 [THREE AXES]).
- [REV v5-cc] **Sense (how finely you perceive) is now the perception side of Skill, not a third dial** (cc R095); the text is kept: (was: "[NEW v5-wk] **THE INNER SENSE (how finely you perceive)** — the third dial, separate from the appendage, trainable and innate (wk W03).") **Basic magic needs only control; deeper levels need finer sense. This is a cost gradient, not a gate** (wk W04) [v5-wk2 attribution: substance is Patrick's — *"To start actually interfering with actual physics you must be able to feel small things"* (chat t65); the words "cost gradient, not a gate" are Claude's (t60, t66)]. Example: the **"numb titan"** — huge Remnant, poor sense (wk W03).
- **EFFORT / FATIGUE (the bill)** — working magic is work; the steward pays mentally and bodily. **Exhaustion is the universal soft limit** — a mage tires like a laborer or a grandmaster. Overreach past what your body and Remnant can pay is dangerous. [NEW v5-cc] **BURNOUT — the body breaks.** Fatigue stays the everyday bill. Burnout is the body breaking when it carries more than it can hold, usually through amplifiers; Remnant can't be destroyed, so it releases when the flesh fails (cc R096). Patrick: "Imagine god channeling his magic and the suit he used is burnt. Thats how you should look at burnout." **RESOLVED v5-cc (cc R096)** — the overdraw question below is closed by burnout. (was: 🌊 whether "overdraw"/burning the self stays a named mechanic is open — the description holds either way [REV v5-wk] — though overdraw can no longer mean burning Remnant, wk W10). *(🌊 The Tower apprentice's death — pushing past his limit and burning from within, `05_POWERS_BANKED.md` — is a story instance of this description; whether it makes "overdraw" a named mechanic is still Patrick's call. See changes file.)* [REV v5-wk] *The apprentice's burning of rift Remnant is overturned by W10; how he dies now needs Patrick's rewrite (W47, clay, keeps only that he kills the queen and dies). 🌊 *Burnout (cc R096) gives his death a mechanic — his body breaking under rift Remnant — but the scene's wording is the apprentice reconcile (B-37), not changed here.**

That is **all** the gating there is [NEW v5-wk] (the inner sense adds cost, not a gate — wk W04) [REV v5-cc] (fine sense is now part of Skill; its cost gradient stands — cc R095). **No physics audit, ever.** We do NOT check whether an act is energetically possible, whether it "needs fusion not weak," mass-budgets, ignition arithmetic, conservation. A weak character can't casually crack a planet — not because math forbids it, but because they lack the Remnant and it would kill them to try. The three soft gates generate every limit a scene needs. **No math** (t72: "your doing math and we agreed no math") — no size charts, no square-cube reasoning, no structural-physics mechanism owed for any being; dragons are the standing proof the world owes no physics mechanism (t73).

> 🚫 **STEER-ONLY RETIRED.** Magic is no longer restricted to "manipulating energy that already exists." It may add energy freely when the scene wants it (unbind an atom and an explosion happens; the energy isn't accounted against a fuel source). Conservation is no longer a rule we enforce. The "Maxwell's-demon / information-work" framing is gone. The only cost is **effort/fatigue**, never an energy ledger.

## Forces & elements = pure descriptive flavor 🔒

- **The four forces (Strong, EM, Weak, Gravity) and the four elements (fire, water, earth, air) are a shared VOCABULARY for describing what magic looked like — applied AFTER the fact, never a system that constrains.** You watch someone unbind an atom and an explosion follows → you call it nuclear. You watch them collapse matter together with great force → you call it gravity. You watch them reshape a thing → EM. You watch them warp *what a thing is* → the weak force. Fire, lightning, freeze, rot, transmutation — all just folk-and-science names for effects.
- **There are NO "users."** No fire-users, no gravity-users, no EM-mages — **no types at all.** There are only **beings who do magic.** Sometimes a being's magic looks like gravity; the next moment the same being does something that looks like fire, or flings a rock with plain momentum, or hardens their skin, or something you wouldn't name. The label names the **act**, never the **person**, never a class, lane, loadout, or kit.
  - **Re-confirmed this session (t612):** "As with all our characters she is just a skilled user." A character who once uses a gravity-looking signature (e.g. the drow's tribute use of Lirael's Collapse, `05_POWERS_BANKED.md`) is **not** a "gravity type." The image names the act.
  - **Re-confirmed (t136):** the "Strong-user" label is **retired** — "Hes just a master." A label that names a category strips the person of the mastery and dedication it took. Strong-flavored feats remain the rarest, found only at the very top of the power scale (t136, t83–84; consistent with Law 7b — mythic by scale and prestige, never a class).
- **Blending is free and unstructured.** Fire + gravity + spin = a fire-gravity tornado, with no permission check. No forced paths, no locked growth trees, no reachability hierarchy, no "EM comes first," no element→force mapping anyone has to obey. Mix and combine whatever the moment calls for.
- **The forces never fuse into a fifth thing** is the only structural residue worth keeping, and even that is just "there are four real fundamental forces in the physics flavor we nod to" — not a rule that gates anyone.
- **Flavor in use — the giants' stone (t29–30, t34):** giant architecture is **grown/willed and seamless**, with no chisel marks; the giants understand complex **chain bonds** to make compounds that let their size stand forever. This is description of mastery (chemistry-flavored), not a mechanism. [REV v5-wk] **Convergence works on bodies** — the funerary version releases the soul; the emperor's version "stoked their bodies as material," and "the remnant is all trapped inside the stone" (wk W15). (was: "The craftsman's power is the *source* used to grow the walls — 'You arent now the walls of a castle your power was the source used to grow the walls themselves' (t34).") 🚫 EM does **not** actively hold a giant's body up (t72). (Giants and Convergence: `07_BEINGS.md`.) [REV v5-wk] (was: "the dead-fueled build" — Remnant cannot be burned or spent, wk W10.)
- [NEW v5-jul] **Machines can mimic magic's effects — never do magic.** Patrick (jul08 t339): "Locked in codex science is just the explanation for magic in a different time period. So humans did the impossible and created technology that can manipulate the same forces we have as our magic system through entirely mechanical means. Controlling electricity through an em field generator that is then turned into the same kinds of magic we see em do." The machine produces a **parallel effect described in the same words, never the same act** (jul08 t340, accepted) — because "Magic is implicitly stated as your conscious manipulating the world" (jul08 t339). A thing with no Remnant (a machine, an ASI) does no magic. *(Who wields such tech, and the human-augment era: `07_BEINGS.md`.)*

## Magic is EXPRESSION, not derivation 🔒 (the core character principle)

**Build the person completely first** — motives, wounds, the delusions they'd defend, their history, who taught them, what they survived, what they'd naturally take to. A whole being, built with no thought to magic. **THEN decide what their magic looks like, as an expression of *that person*.** Flavor (force/element) is assigned **last**, to describe the output — never to derive or explain the character.

- **No derivation in EITHER direction.** Not ability→character ("she wields gravity, so she's patient"). Not character→ability ("he's angry, so he must be fire"). Not race→element, not temperament→affinity, not nature+ability+element+race as any equation. All retired.
- **The "why this magic" is ALWAYS the individual's life** — what this specific person learned, leaned into, and felt drawn to — **never the element's supposed temperament.** Fifty people whose magic sometimes looks like "earth" are fifty different people for fifty different reasons; they are not all patient, because "earth" has no temperament to impose.
- **The same effect can mean opposite things in two beings.** One person's gravity is grief (heaviness, surrender, letting go); another's is dominance (crushing, pinning). Same described effect, opposite souls — because the magic is downstream of the person. A type-system can't do this; ours gets it for free.
- This is the No-Formula / "silence on the soul" discipline (`12_METHOD.md`) applied to magic: the system defines what magic IS and then **stays silent about who people are.** It does not grant *abilities* an identity, let alone people.
- [NEW v5-jul] **Every character develops their own powers; gods are the ultimate expression.** Patrick (jul23 t106): "Characters developing their own unique powers uses our system to its fullest degree... create truly unique flavor for every being. God's take this to the ultimate expression in the series." A god's magic is not a different system — Patrick rolled back his own idea that gods "practice magic that is different to remnant" (jul23 t104); it is the same Remnant magic, carried to its furthest individual expression. (A god's signature technique offered through a pact: `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`.)

## People are not types — but they ARE individuals 🔒 (the texture)

Loosening the system does NOT make everyone an identical infinitely-fluid blank. People have **histories, tastes, strengths, and specialties** — they're just not *classes*. (Wheel of Time is the cleaner comp than Harry Potter: one undivided Power, but every channeler has natural strengths, favorite weaves, things they never learned, things their gift makes easy — individual expression of a single source, real differences in *kind and scale*, without anyone being a "Fire person.")
- **Learned repertoire:** a being knows the workings they bothered to learn; leans on what comes naturally; reaches for something else when forced. Repertoire flows from **their life and choices**, not a label the system stamped.
- **Natural inclination (in kind and scale):** talent suits some things to some people; some workings come easily, some never. Culture/disposition may *color* what someone gravitates toward (a war-forged person reaches for war-shaped magic) — but it's **pressure, never a wall, always individual** (statistical flavor at most).
- **Chosen specialty:** mastery, preference, study, and "what came naturally" are all real and differentiating — they're just downstream of the person.
- **Magic isn't the only learnable art.** Potions, enchantment, craft, lore, the non-magical disciplines sit alongside it (a "potions master" isn't a different kind of mage — just someone who went deep on a craft). This gives low-Remnant and non-prodigy characters somewhere to be excellent, and the world schools/trades/depth. (Enchantment as a craft → `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`.)

## The Awakening Gradient 🔒 (kept, simplified)

Magic ability is **"how far along am I?"**, never on/off — a continuous gradient of **control + understanding**: involuntary leaks (power escaping unaimed, loudest under emotion) → crude intent → control through understanding → engineered reproducible workings → mastery.
- Your **Remnant (fragment size) sets the CEILING** [REV v5-cc] **of your own capacity**, capped by your body; added capacity (devices, grafted flesh, a held soul) raises what you can hold, at the body's risk (cc R097, R096) (was: "sets the CEILING" unqualified); practice sets how far you travel; it dulls with neglect, deepens with use. Sapience is the visible readout of having enough fragment to begin.
- [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **Practice never adds Remnant:** "unlike some games you dont gain mana over time" (Patrick, BANK 11-16). A being's own Remnant does not grow with training or age. *(His word "mana" means capacity here; the 🚫 mana-as-pool tripwire stands.)* (cc R022)
- Individual, never racial (only statistically race-flavored, since fragment-size distributions differ).

## Spells 🔒 (kept)

**Spells** = specific, complex, **reproducible** workings — engineered by understanding deeply enough to combine effects precisely (the magical equivalent of a repeatable experiment). Taught by teaching fundamentals + how they combine, then drilling reproduction. **NOT slotted/plug-and-play.** Capped by Remnant, accessed by skill, no hard cap on number known. Makes authored signature moves, schools, lineages, hoarded/lost spells, and "she knows X but not Y" all structurally real.

## Soul magic — the rare second branch 🔒 (same Remnant, different rules)
*[REV v5-wk] (was: "(same fuel, different rules)" — Remnant cannot be burned or spent, wk W10.)*

Spirit usually grips **matter** — dead physics with no fragment, which can't push back, the "safe" target (everything above). Rarely, a being turns Spirit on **another fragment of the One** — mind, memory, emotion, will, the soul itself. [REV v5-wk] Same Remnant and effort (was: "Same fuel (your own Remnant + effort)"), but the rules are completely different because you're touching **living consciousness that touches back.**
- **No forces, no elements, no physics-flavor** — it's **will against will, coherence against coherence.**
- **Two-way and intimate:** what you grip can grip you. The limiter is **self-risk, not fatigue** — overreach and you bleed the other's nature into yours, fracture, or lose pieces of self (the same way soul-harvesting already fragments you). *(Holding a bound soul adds a separate, constant cost — see Soul-binding below.)*
- **Rare** because most beings only ever learn to grip matter; turning the hand inward on another fragment is profound and dangerous. It is also **forbidden and scarcely known** (t544).
- **Belongs to no race.** (t484 — "there's no reason any race cannot learn soul magic and begin binding their remnant to others. Nothing makes this a human domain.") Law 8: nothing is locked to any people.
- **Tempting and taboo.** (t680.) Everyone knows souls can be stolen and transferred 🌊 *(what the public knows of its own tech and the tainted cores: NEEDS_PATRICK, Pass 2026-11 open calls, B-41)*; that knowledge is what makes the art both tempting and taboo. "Some people are so evil they will steal everything you have including your soul."
- [NEW v5-jul] **It can override a living Remnant and take the body.** Patrick (jul08 t329): "how else would another human use soul magic to invade and take their body over without that implicit ability in our system to override someone's remnant and steal their body." Compare the transfer road of soul theft (below, t676): forcing your own soul onto another body. *(Claude's "domination" naming for an override that leaves the victim's fragment in place was never confirmed — changes file.)*
- [NEW v5-wk] **Stealing production** — taking others' Remnant; [REV v5-wk2] [REV v5-cc] the mechanism is an amplifier — "I think its an amplifier only" (BANK 10-31); "drives their grip" retires (cc R132) (was: "the mechanism is 🌊 open — the thief driving their grip, or 'using an amplifier to touch a wider pool' (Patrick, chat t83: 'Im not sure')") (was: "the thief drives their grip" — Claude's t84 framing, never confirmed) (wk W11).
- [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **A held soul can be forced to work.** Besides extending your own reach, "you can just grab them and force them to do it also" (Patrick, BANK 10-31; the 10-31 follow-up revised only the battery half) (cc R035).
- [REV v5-cc] **The elven bond is an extrasensory organ through which elves feel one another — not soul magic, not a tether, and it shares no Remnant** (cc R098). Patrick: "Yes elves just have an extrasensory organ they feel one another its not a tether"; "elves never sensed each other's souls they just read the bond which is a sensory organ. The organ is gone if their remnant is just inside the blade" (BANK 11-09). Its reach scales with Remnant and distance: "A single elf far flung has such a tiny pinprick… the home world… would shine like a beacon… up close… you would feel the elves and they would feel you" (BANK 11-01). (was: "[NEW v5-wk] **The elven bond is innate, constant, collective, and unique to elves**; elves are the premier sensors, and the elf queen's 'vigilance' comes from intense use of the bond (wk W07). **The bond does NOT track individuals** — an elf who dies far away dies alone, without the bond (wk W08).") Innate, constant, collective and unique to elves still stands; the queen's vigilance is intense use of the organ.
- [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **Pressure fields and immunity.** A powerful being exerting itself presses on everyone near it: "to even have consious thought when the being is exerting power is to also have these natural defenses… yiu need to develope shields to certain types of pressure." Physical immunity is the same thing: "Concentrated continuous exertion that requires massive remnant and control to maintain keeps this force barrier of psychic power around them" (Patrick, BANK 11-16 [WORLD · pressure fields]); "soul pressure" (BANK 11-16 [DERREK · unleashed]). A target's defenses resist fine-control influence (Derrek's, `08`) (cc R067).
- [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **Fine control reaches the body's chemistry** — cells, hormones, pheromones, blood pressure read as mood, and nudged (Patrick, BANK 11-16 [DERREK · fine control]; `08` DERREK) (cc R066). 🌊 Whether that influence is matter magic or soul magic is not stated.
- 🌊 Specifics (named workings, exact effects) are **discovered per scene**, grounded in this frame — never pre-catalogued.

### Echoes, ghosts, and changelings — three different things ✅ (t498–502) *(verify fix: all five 🔒 stamps on these new soul-magic subsections are now ✅. Patrick confirmed the material, but nothing in t498–513 or t676 locks it.)*

- **ECHOES** — loose Remnant left by great death (battlefields, sieges, massacres). **Impressions only; no person is there.** They fade back into the pool over centuries. Places of great death are ghost-sites. 🌊 *Accepted in substance (t500) but tied to the open reservoir question: dense unclaimed Remnant at such sites as a resource for soul-mages, changelings and reservoir builders ("a massacre site is a mine," t499) — see changes file.*
- **GHOSTS** — "a ghost would be remnant which was bound together by magic" (Patrick, t500). Remnant deliberately held together so a dead self cannot disperse. **Every true ghost is a soul-binding crime; a haunting is a crime scene.** Ghosts may be bound as guardians, servants, power sources, punishment — or out of love.
- **CHANGELINGS** — many souls bound into one living driver (`07_BEINGS.md`).
- [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **When the body can't hold it, Remnant goes back to the world.** "The remnant is fine. It just releases back into the environment because your body no longer retains the required structures to hold remnant" (Patrick, BANK 11-16). Released, never destroyed. (cc R024)
- 🌊 **Whether a self survives death, and where it goes, stays open by design** (t499).
- A bound soul has "some type of experience" — but full experience "takes biology" (t42, Patrick). [REV v5-jul] Patrick's July image fits this: a soul held with no working brain is left in "the same sort of existential dread a soul that was stolen and trapped inside an artifact must feel without the processors to actually understand" (jul08 t341). Beyond that, what it is like to be held is left unresolved. *(was: "What it is like to be held is left unresolved.")* [NEW v5-wk] Ruled: **a bound soul feels something — [REV v5-cc] only vague, general things, maybe some strangeness — "sensation comes from sensory organs" (BANK 11-02); dread is flavor, not the rule (cc R128) (was: "dread, without a brain to understand it")** (wk W13).
- [NEW v5-wk] **Undead types:** plague (biotech); animated flesh; souls bound to corpses; souls in machines; changeling leftovers (wk W69). **Resurrection is possible in principle** — decoherence: nothing destroyed, odds near zero (wk W51).
- **Not every walking corpse is a ghost.** The Orc King's dead are **empty**: dead flesh animated with no soul held in it — "maybe he isnt capable of holding soul to flesh but he can animate just the flesh itself" (t522). Contrast the holding arts below, whose works are full of trapped people. (Orc King: `08_CHARACTERS.md`; his pact: `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`.)

### Soul-binding is CONCENTRATION — the holder pays ✅ (t504–505)

- [NEW v5-wk] **Scope, per W14: ghosts need a holder; objects hold souls without a holder's concentration** (wk W14) [REV v5-wk2: 🌊 proposed, unconfirmed — Claude's proposal (chat t82); Patrick moved on and never addressed it]. The concentration rule below is the ghost's rule; a soul held in an object is enchantment (wk W12; `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`).
- Patrick (t504): "What if the cost is a constant effort to hold the magic still." **A binding is never finished.** The holder must keep holding, every day; **the holder pays.**
- **Kill the holder and the binding lapses** — the held soul is [REV v5-cc] freed, its Remnant released back into the world, never destroyed (cc R096, R024) (was: "freed or destroyed"). Patrick's example: "the death of the living brother leads to his magic lapsing and both brothers being lost in the same tragic move." This is also a tactic: to free or end a ghost, kill whoever holds it.
- The same rule reads on changelings: one driver holding a crowd by constant will — the noise in their minds [NEW v5-wk] — a guardrail that holds **only for changelings who keep a sustainable pace** (wk W22). [REV v5-wk] (was: "and why a changeling who spends every stolen soul has nothing left to hold (the Tower changeling's silence, `08_CHARACTERS.md`)" — Remnant cannot be burned or spent, wk W10; the Tower changeling scene needs revising in `08`/`09`.)
- [REV v5-wk] Contrast: **Convergence works on bodies** — the funerary version **releases** the soul; the emperor's version **trapped the city's Remnant in the stone** (wk W15). (was: "**Convergence is spent, not held** — 'mostly its burnt to build' (t42): the dead giant's soul is burned into the working (`07_BEINGS.md`).")

### Warden-objects (placeholder term) — deliberately hand-wavey ✅ (concept) / 🌊 (mechanism) (t506–509)

- A ghost that lasts thousands of years needs "an even sicker use of soul magic meets enchantment. Where you bind someone's soul permanently to an object and force its only purpose to be maintaining concentration on the ghost" (Patrick, t506).
- So an ancient haunting has **two victims**: the ghost, and the hidden warden-soul holding it. **Breaking the warden's object frees both.**
- The object is the anchor; the matter itself never becomes alive or gains a soul of its own (Law 0c stands — reconciliation per t507; see changes file). [NEW v5-wk] Under W12 the object *holds* the warden-soul — that is enchantment, [REV v5-cc] Remnant held inside something (cc R099) (was: "a soul held in matter"); the matter does no magic, the held soul does. Objects hold souls without a holder's concentration (wk W12, W14) [REV v5-wk2: the W14 half is 🌊 proposed, unconfirmed — Claude's proposal, chat t82].
- **Firm parts:** a ghost needs a holder; holding costs the holder; breaking the holder frees the ghost. **The mechanism stays an unquantified dark art** — "This one is slightly hand wavey but ghost magic isnt easy to quantify anyway" (t508).

### The vessel varies — holding is the art ✅ (t510–513)

- The core mechanic is **the act of holding**, not undeath. "We happened to use his body this time. But we could lock him into an amulet like the son. Or armor like al." (t512.) The vessel can be the dead person's own body, an amulet, armor — any vessel. **The necromancer's craft = the holding + the vessel.** [NEW v5-wk] Body-like substrate holds best (wk W12). 🌊 Under W14 (objects hold souls without concentration; ghosts need a holder — [REV v5-wk2] itself 🌊 proposed, unconfirmed: Claude's proposal, chat t82), which of these vessels need a holder is not stated — flagged.
- 🟡 Example in canon (t510): a family captured by a dark Returned necromancer, who forges the son into an amulet bound to the dead father's chest to keep the father cohered, because the mother couldn't lose her husband. When she dies of old age, the husband is left with the memory and his dead son keeping him cohered.
- Touchstone: binding a loved one's soul into armor (Patrick, t502).

### The two roads of soul theft ✅ (t676)

"There are 2 ways to become a changeling. You move body or consume them."
- **TRANSFER** — force your own soul into another body and leave the old one behind. "If your a really old man when you finally gain the ability you would likely force your soul on a younger body."
- **CONSUME** — take souls into your own body and keep it. "If your some type of ancient being like a dragon or you have some type of limited bloodline trait you would be more likely to consume souls into your body."
- **A crime, not a race** (t680): "changelings arent some race they have to worry about. Its your father its your uncle its the priest at the church." Anyone of any race can commit it.
- [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **A soul cannot be sold.** "You cant sell a soul… You can sell a being. You can bind their soul to something and sell that. You can mine the natural remnant and force it to work but its not a currency" (Patrick, BANK 11-02) (cc R033).
- **Only the powerful can.** Becoming a changeling takes "a sufficiently powerful user who is well versed enough in soul magic a forbidden and scarcely known type of magic. ALL CHANGELINGS ARE INCREDIBLY POWERFUL OFF RIP." (t544.)
- [NEW v5-wk] **Pace and the tell.** Changelings take **1–2 souls at a time** (wk W16). The **soul–body mismatch** is the tell; the smart ones shield it or hop to bigger bodies (wk W18). Failure modes: the giant's **decay** and the young dark elf's **rupture** (wk W20). Changelings are now largely monsters (wk W19).
- Changeling detail (both roads in practice, tactics, psychology): `07_BEINGS.md`.

### Wholesale absorption — gated by power, worked by coherence [NEW v5-jul] ⚖️ (jul23 t116–120; Patrick-stated, never explicitly locked)

- **Slow siphoning is retired; full absorption is not.** Patrick (jul23 t116): "if remnant isnt transferable aka slowly schiponed doesn't necessarily stop full possession. We already know changelings can meld a chunk of remnant to their own wholesale."
- **Power-gated, not kind-gated.** (jul23 t118): "It requires a being as strong as a changeling to even preform the act but one as powerful as a god can do it on larger scales orders of magnitude greater on many at once." (jul23 t120): "A dragon or a giant who uses spirit magic would also be able to do this." Any being strong enough and versed in soul magic can — **Jon and Derrek included** (jul23 t119–120: "exactly what I was gonna say is the direct implication").
- **The mechanism is coherence.** (jul23 t118): "the distinction is the remnants ability to stay coherent in the presence of a greater remnant... when a god absorbs a lesser being... their own coherence is lost to the swirl of the gods own remnant."
- This is soul-harvesting seen from the taker's side (`03_COSMOLOGY.md`, Constitution 14): it raises the taker's Remnant and pluralizes them. [NEW v5-wk] The rulings' name for taking others' Remnant: **stealing their production — [REV v5-wk2] [REV v5-cc] the mechanism is an amplifier — "I think its an amplifier only" (BANK 10-31); "drives their grip" retires (cc R132) (was: "the mechanism is 🌊 open — the thief driving their grip, or 'using an amplifier to touch a wider pool' (Patrick, chat t83: 'Im not sure')") (was: "the thief drives their grip" — Claude's t84 framing, never confirmed)** (wk W11). The consume road of soul theft (above) is its changeling form. *(A god's will-control of a thrall and pact-related absorption: `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`.)*

### What soul magic unifies (cross-references)

- **Soul-binding and soul-harvesting** (`03_COSMOLOGY.md`, Constitution 14) — the deepest violations; [REV v5-cc] harvesting is one way to hold more Remnant than your own, beside devices and grafted flesh (cc R097) (was: "harvesting remains the only way to raise innate Remnant"), and it fragments/pluralizes you.
- **Convergence** — [REV v5-wk] works on bodies: the funerary version releases the soul; the emperor's version trapped the city's Remnant in the stone (wk W15). The original Convergence was god-forging; its lost secret, silencing the crowd into unison, is **"soul mortar"** (wk W17). (was: "harvest into a *working*: a dead soul burned as the source of a will-imposed build (a third application beside binding and harvesting into a living being)".) `07_BEINGS.md`.
- [REV v5-cc] **Enchantment** — **simply Remnant held inside something, in many uses and forms** (cc R099). (was: "[NEW v5-wk] **Enchantment** — a soul held in matter (wk W12)") Objects hold souls without a holder's concentration (wk W14) [REV v5-wk2: 🌊 proposed, unconfirmed — Claude's proposal (chat t82); Patrick moved on and never addressed it]. `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`.
- [REV v5-cc] **The elven bond is no longer listed here as soul magic: it is a sensory organ, not a tether, sharing no Remnant** (cc R098). 🌊 Whether the July will-binding survives as something done up close through the organ is not ruled. Patrick's July words stay on record: "A strong elf has a natural ability to bind other elves to its will" (jul23 t132); "Binding their will isnt as total but this is the mechanism we just built for the pacts. I dont mean they destroy their coherence" (jul23 t134); the bond lets elves feel a member's disposition (jul23 t132; elven authoritarianism: `07_BEINGS.md`). Innate, constant, collective and unique to elves still stands (wk W07). (was: "**The elven bond** — [REV v5-jul] a gentle passive form, and a weaponized one… [NEW v5-wk] Innate, constant, collective, unique to elves; it does **not** track individuals (wk W07, W08). 🌊 How 'thought monitoring' reads beside W08 is flagged for Patrick." — W08 is retired by cc R098.)
- **Pacts** — a pact is soul magic: "Giving a pact would be the reverse of when they take a soul. Instead connecting to them and opening that flow" (t666). Under the July pact rework (approved t630), pacts grant **technique, never Remnant**, and bind the [REV v5-jul] pact-holder *(was: "the mortal" — Patrick, jul23 t118: "careful not to call them mortal gods are mortals")* to the patron by a soul-magic tether. Full frame: `06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`.
- **Jon's alien Remnant** making the Orc King's demon *flinch* (`08_CHARACTERS.md`).
- [NEW v5-jul] **Wholesale absorption** — the power-gated extreme of the branch (section above; jul23 t116–120).
- **Changelings** — the art's most feared practitioners (`07_BEINGS.md`); angels and demons stand further along the same blurred continuum (`07_BEINGS.md`).
- **The Returned** fuse soul magic with enchantment and the maze's warping into one dreaded craft (t514; `07_BEINGS.md`).
- [REV v5-wk] **Spending stolen souls — RULED OUT.** "we cant burn remnant": Remnant cannot be burned or spent; any line saying a being "burns all his stolen souls" must be revised (wk W10). Taking others' Remnant is stealing their production (wk W11); Convergence works on bodies (wk W15). (was: "🌊 **Spending stolen souls.** Canon now has a changeling burning its stolen souls to power an attack (t342, t774) and Convergence burning a dead soul into a build (t36, t42) … flagged for Patrick (changes file), not settled here.")

## Power scale 🔒 (pure continuum)

Power is a single graded scale of [REV v5-cc] **Remnant, Will, Skill × time-to-learn** (cc R095) (was: "**Remnant × skill × time-to-learn**"). "Demigod" / "god" are descriptive points on it, NOT gated tiers. A weak god vastly exceeds mortals but ranks low among gods. Given enough Remnant and time, a mortal simply becomes a god — which is exactly what eternity made of Jon & Derrek.
- **Gods are what happens when ANY user becomes incredibly powerful** (t668) — by either road: matter ("a being who perfected gravity magic to harden their body beyond stone or an em specialist who can twist mater at a whim," t670) or soul (angels and demons are soul-magic users, t668).
- **No graduation.** Changeling, angel/demon and god are blurred regions on one continuum — "You dont just graduate from changeling school and your now an angel and where the line again becomes god is murkier still" (t674). Angel and demon are one kind of being (t674). Detail: `07_BEINGS.md`.
- [NEW v5-wk] **Roads and no formula.** All gods are born of flesh, on one world (wk W30). [REV v5-cc] **Any being of any size can become a god given enough time and practice**; theft and the keeper's pact are shortcuts (BANK 11-01; cc R107). (was: "Humans reach godhood only by **time-fusion** (Jon, Derrek) **or theft**; dragons, giants and elves can grow singular (wk W31).") Singular gods revile changelings, but power earns respect regardless; behavior is individual — **no formula ties god vs. demon to method of ascent**; a changeling who ascended is not a "god" in the singular sense (wk W32). The greatest giant god is a million minds in unison (wk W17).

## LIFE / DEATH 🌊 (a soul-magic flavor)
- Growth, decay, fertility, disease, the living process; necromancy, ghosts, soul-passage. Sits on the **soul-magic** branch (acting on the living fragment, not on dead matter). Likely the most evocative use of soul magic on the page.
- **Now partly built (v5) — see `04_MAGIC_SUBSTRATE.md`, soul magic:** echoes vs. ghosts vs. changelings are distinct (t498–502); a ghost is Remnant bound together by magic, and every true ghost is a soul-binding crime; soul-binding is **concentration** — the holder pays, and killing the holder frees or destroys the ghost (t504–505); long-lived ghosts are held by **warden-objects**, deliberately hand-wavey (t506–509); **necromancy = the holding + the vessel** — body, amulet, armor (t510–513).
- Not soul magic: the Orc King's dead are empty flesh animated with no soul in it (t522; `08_CHARACTERS.md`).
- [NEW v5-jul] A held soul with no working brain feels only vague "existential dread," like "a soul that was stolen and trapped inside an artifact... without the processors to actually understand" (jul08 t341; `04`).
- [NEW v5-wk] **Ruled:** a bound soul feels [REV v5-cc] only vague, general things, maybe some strangeness — "sensation comes from sensory organs" (BANK 11-02); dread is flavor, not the rule (cc R128) (was: "dread, without a brain to understand it") (wk W13). [REV v5-wk2] (was listed under "Ruled") 🌊 *Proposed, unconfirmed:* objects hold souls without a holder's concentration; ghosts need a holder (wk W14 — Claude's proposal, chat t82; Patrick moved on and never addressed it). [REV v5-cc] **Enchantment is simply Remnant held inside something, in many uses and forms** (cc R099). (was: "**Enchantment = a soul held in matter** (wk W12).")
- [NEW v5-wk] **Undead types:** plague (biotech); animated flesh; souls bound to corpses; souls in machines; changeling leftovers (wk W69).
- [NEW v5-wk] **Resurrection is possible in principle** — decoherence: nothing destroyed, odds near zero; [REV v5-cc] no one can trace them back — "Its to hard to find vague specs of remnant long since swirled back into the world" (BANK 11-07; cc R122) (was: "Derrek, who sees time, could trace the fragments (wk W51).").
- *Status:* rules above are banked; everything else discovered per scene; no pre-spec. 🌊 Whether a self survives death, and where it goes, stays open by design (t499).

## MIND 🌊 (core soul magic)
- Affecting minds directly — cognition, memory, emotion, perception, will. This **IS soul magic** (Spirit gripping another's Remnant): will-vs-will, two-way, limited by self-risk. Not a separate domain — it's the central case of the rare branch.
- 🟡 Example in canon (t342): the Tower changeling uses "ultimate disillusionment magic he cultivated over his very long lifespan to try and overwhelm derreks soul and take him," [REV v5-wk] ⚠️ (was: "burning through the souls locked inside him until every last one is gone") — **overturned: Remnant cannot be burned or spent** (wk W10); how the attack now plays is for the scene's home files; Derrek stands "still as coherent as ever." (Scene: `08_CHARACTERS.md` / `09_STRUCTURE.md`.)
- [NEW v5-wk] **Sensing other beings' Remnant** is a rare master-level skill — "Some very talented masters have learned to sense other beings remnant. This is rare" (wk W07). It comes from the inner sense (wk W03) [REV v5-cc] — now part of Skill, not a dial (cc R095). On the page: rare, felt rather than reported, unreliable — never "video gamey" (wk W09). [v5-verify-wk: 🌊 "felt rather than reported" and "unreliable" are Claude's specifics (chat t226), unconfirmed; rarity and anti-"video gamey" are Patrick's (t223, t225) — L35.] The elven bond is innate, constant, collective and unique to elves, and does not track individuals (wk W07, W08). [REV v5-cc] The bond is a sensory organ, not soul-sensing; its reach scales with Remnant and distance (cc R098). (was: "does not track individuals".)
- [NEW v5-wk] **Stealing production** — taking others' Remnant; [REV v5-wk2] [REV v5-cc] the mechanism is an amplifier — "I think its an amplifier only" (BANK 10-31); "drives their grip" retires (cc R132) (was: "the mechanism is 🌊 open — the thief driving their grip, or 'using an amplifier to touch a wider pool' (Patrick, chat t83: 'Im not sure')") (was: "the thief drives their grip" — Claude's t84 framing, never confirmed) (wk W11).
- [NEW v5-jul] **Now partly built — see `04_MAGIC_SUBSTRATE.md`, soul magic:** overriding a living Remnant to take its body (jul08 t329); a strong elf binding a weaker elf's will through the bond, never total (jul23 t132, t134); wholesale absorption, power-gated, worked by coherence (jul23 t116–120). A god's puppet-control of a thrall is pact material (`06_EXTERNAL_POWERS.md`; jul23 t122).
- *Status:* discovered per scene.

## PACTS — the deal-with-a-being umbrella 🔒 (reworked v5 — the July pact rework, approved "all good" [t630])
**Every "deal with a powerful being for power" is a Pact** — there is no separate system for blessings vs. blood rituals vs. demon deals vs. divine-domain channeling. They differ only by **patron** and **price**, not by mechanism.
- **The mechanism (v5):** **a pact grants TECHNIQUE, never Remnant** — the patron gives the [REV v5-jul] (was: "mortal") pact-holder **its own way of doing magic**, not raw power [t629/t630, t633–634]. [REV v5-verify] (was: "The pact-holder's own soul pays for every use" — Claude's t629 summary wording, retired in Constitution 16) **The pact-holder pays for every use from their own limited Remnant — the same effort/fatigue every act of magic costs** (jul23 t108, Patrick picked this option). A **soul-magic tether** binds the pact-holder to the patron — fading on the pact-holder's side, never on the patron's [t629/t630]. *(This replaces the old soul-siphon pacts — see RETIRED.)*
  - [NEW v5-jul] **Each patron's technique is its own signature** — Patrick: patrons "have developed kekegenki and can imbue a user with their own specific brand of magic they developed with the help of their massive remnant… it will look unique for each god who imbues a user" (jul23 t106). Gods take characters-developing-their-own-unique-powers "to the ultimate expression in the series" (jul23 t106).
  - [NEW v5-jul] **Remnant never transfers** — Patrick: "remnant isn't transferable. They cant give their remnant they only give the knowledge or ability to use it. This also limits how crazy the characters can be. A user in book 1 using a gods remnant would be undefeatable. A user using a gods power with their own limited remnant keeps them grounded" (jul23 t108; siphon removal ordered jul23 t114). **A pact doesn't make you strong; it makes you unrepeatable** — opening the link is the real bargain, and the technique is then bounded by your own Remnant and effort (jul23 t109, accepted).
  - [NEW v5-jul] **A patron must be strong enough to support the link** (Patrick: they "can offer a pact because they are strong enough with remnant to support the link", jul23 t106). *(July said "only gods"; under the physics chat the ones who hand out pacts are superior soul mages — angels/demons/changelings — and "god" is a level of power [t666, t668]. Whether blood rituals and Blight-patrons meet this bar was never ruled — see changes file.)*
  - **A pact is a harvest reversed** (Patrick): "Giving a pact would be the reverse of when they take a soul. Instead connecting to them and opening that flow" [t666]. Who could hand out pacts "if not a superior soul mage who had control over using and manipulating souls?" [t666].
  - [REV v5-jul] (was: "Still the equalizer: a weak being can cast far past what it is…") A weak being can still reach **far past what it is** — but only by paying from its own limited Remnant (effort/fatigue, Constitution 16; jul23 t108) — the pact grants no extra Remnant. [REV v5-xfile] (was: "…paying from its own small soul, so it **burns itself out** doing it (the Orc King's shape) [t633–634]" — that phrasing is Claude's t633 summary, which Patrick saved for later at t634 without confirming, and it clashes with the Constitution's retired BURNOUT tripwire; 🌊 whether over-reaching ends in burnout is open.) Unstable; **someone holds the leash.**
  - [NEW v5-jul] **Taught abilities remain** — Patrick: "even as the link to the god diminishes the taught abilities remain" (jul23 t114).
  - [NEW v5-jul] **How the patron collects — the asymmetric tether:** the soul-magic grip is fragile on the pact-holder's side (it needs attunement and fades) but costs the patron nothing, so the patron can always find the pact-holder and collect: "You can stop attuning. You can't stop being findable." What a patron does when it collects (a demand, a planted curse or geas) is decided per patron (jul23 t115, accepted; written after the t136 go-ahead).
  - Borrowed effects used alongside innate magic interfere; used in bursts. *(Pre-rework detail, kept pending check — see changes file.)*
- **How a patron takes hold of you** (Patrick): **"A god asks for your devotion. A demon offers you a deal."** [t548]
  - [NEW v5-jul] **Reaching a patron through attunement** — Patrick: "as the user attuned themselves with the remnant in the universe they discover these beings. They appear in the ether as the bhudda…"; a user "can literally be weakened by losing enlightenment"; "the user is taught the technique. The god teaches them better control of remnant through secrets they hold from their long life" (jul23 t112). The link fades if attunement lapses (jul23 t114). 🌊 Whether losing attunement also costs coherence is open (Claude's proposal, jul23 t113).
  - [NEW v5-jul] **No binary:** what separates one patron's pact from another's, and what it demands, "is dependent on the specific diety. I dont think we should decide what they would be as a binary" (jul23 t110).
  - [NEW v5-wk] **Religion as recruitment.** A religion is a portrait of its god and a recruitment network of **pact champions** — **the tether feeds the god.** There are faith priests, pact priests, and One-intuiting mystics (wk W57). Religion = the name versus the act (wk W57).

  - **Angels / demons** — **one kind of being** ("Angel and demon is the same… The line is far more blurred") [t674]. **They are the same as changelings** — soul mages, the beings most able to use and manipulate souls, hence the ones who can hand out pacts [t666, t668]. **No graduation:** "You dont just graduate from changeling school and your now an angel" — changeling, angel/demon and god are blurred regions on one continuum, and where it becomes god "is murkier still" [t674]. ## Threshold-beings / In-betweeners (Tier-3) 🔒 lineage · ⚖️ mechanics
*An ancient lineage pre-dating the One (not descended from it), in their own bubble between the worlds; obey physics, run the Rule-OS, not Remnant.*
> [REV v5-jul] (was: whole section stamped 🔒) **Stability tier (Patrick, jul08 t365):** the lineage and OS above stay locked (Constitution 15). The power mechanics below — Phase-step, Unfixing, the Hold, the emergency ladder and Cascade, the Afflicted/Victor split — are Claude Code's formalization of Patrick's general description ("rule beasts moving outside of our reality because they exist outside it"): "they sound good and can always be adjusted later for scenes." They are an approved, **adjustable foundation (⚖️)**, not fixed law. The Void, Chain, two states and splitting are Patrick's own later descriptions (physics chat) — canon, but never locked.
[NEW v5-wk] **In-betweeners stay alien and separate; they are the Qu-like remakers** (wk W37).
**Fuel = transition (change/becoming). Price = coherence.** (v5: the death that coherence buys is **splitting too far to come back** — see Splitting.) They operate **outside** the Remnant/force system (they predate it) — they don't out-power anyone, they **sidestep** the rules. Powers are narrow, specific, **rule-shaped.**

**THE VOID** (v5; 🔒 removed v5-jul — never locked) [t126–131, t430] — **the Void is the space around the in-betweener** (Patrick): "they arent moving through our dimension at all. They are moving their void to where they want it." An in-betweener is never actually standing in our dimension; what looks like one present in a room is its Void brought to that place ("they bring the bubble to you") [t130–131]. **The Void is their little pocket where you play the Rule** [t128]. **It exists on top of the real world** — laid over real rooms or real land — so those inside may **not realize at first** that anything has changed [t430]. Outsiders can't simply break into it: "its an ambiguous moving zone attached to a in betweener" [t146].

**CHAIN** (v5; 🔒 removed v5-jul — never locked) [t126, t130] — **the ability to bind;** Chain **drags the victim into the Void.** Distinct from the Hold (below).

**CHAIN VOID** (v5; 🔒 removed v5-jul — never locked) [t126] — "the natural result of fusing the two." **Void, Chain and Chain Void are GENERAL in-betweener powers,** not one being's signature ("I like it being a general power") [t126].

**TWO STATES** (v5; 🔒 removed v5-jul — never locked) [t132] — "inside void they have no true form. They are as ethereal and unreal as the void dimension they live in. However perhaps they can choose to leave the void momentarily and assume a physical form." *(Session reading, accepted by continuation [t133]: this is the domain Constitution 4b means — deathless within its own Void; a manifested body outside it obeys physics and can be pinned — fits "Unfixing countered by being pinned.")*

**SPLITTING** (v5; 🔒 removed v5-jul — never locked) [t164] — "A rule beast can split into as many forms as they like however the more they become the more decohered they are until they choose to reassemble. Go too far form too many and they can never remember who they were to return." Each split thins coherence; pieces can reassemble while enough self remains to remember; past that point the pieces drift on not knowing they were one being — **their true death** [t164–165]. A keeper can leave its seat this way, sending out pieces while its core stays [t164–165]. *(Patrick: this is the same mechanic the One uses — it decohered into everything and can't pull back together; the Law of the Regress lives in `03_COSMOLOGY.md` [t166]. A shared law of selves, not shared lineage — in-betweeners remain a separate lineage [t167].)*

**Universal kit (true in-betweeners)** ⚖️ [REV v5-jul] (adjustable foundation, jul08 t365):
- **Phase-step** — transition-based movement (cheap short, costly far). *(v5 reading, accepted by continuation: phase-step is the in-betweener repositioning its Void's point of contact with our world — far contact costs more than near [t131].)*
- **Unfixing** — a flicker of non-presence; defense; can't be sustained; countered by being **pinned** (e.g. a gravity anchor).
- **Threshold-sense** — passive perception of transitions/seams/instability and of other transitional beings (incl. Jon & Derrek); free.
- **Minor reshaping** — cheap small-scale state-change.
- **The Hold** — force something to *stay* mid-transition (their trap/prison signature); bleeds coherence continuously → the encounter clock. *(Hold arrests a state; Chain drags a body into the Void.)*
- **Void / Chain / Chain Void** — above.

**The Rule** ⚖️ [REV v5-jul] (was 🔒; jul08 t365 — the concept is Patrick's, its formal mechanics adjustable) — a **binding condition/law imposed on a bounded space that traps everyone inside it — the in-betweener included.** Releases only when its condition is met (e.g. "only one may leave"). **(v5) The bounded space is the Void** — the Rule is played inside the in-betweener's pocket, laid over real rooms or real land [t128, t154, t430]. The in-betweener is bound by its own law and must win its own game to survive it. The fight is a **puzzle-prison:** deduce the wording, navigate/survive it, defeat or escape the hunter who works the same rules against you.
- **Bound, not trapped** (v5, Patrick) [t160]: for an in-betweener master of its own condition, "leaving is not hard. He is here because its his web. It is hard for a fly to leave the spiders web while the spider dances around preparing for dinner."
- **They choose their contests** (Patrick) [t160]: "rule beasts tend not to take challenges they do not feel confident they can beat."
- Those who meet the condition are simply released — "naturally excused by the rule beast so they arent kept" [t622].

**Emergency moves (tiered)** ⚖️ [REV v5-jul] (jul08 t365): Lash-Out (overload unfixing) → Sacrifice-Step (tear free of a pin by abandoning coherence; escape diminished) → Snare-Reversal (hold the attacker's pin mid-transition; coherence-vs-Remnant race) → Anchor-Theft (transition the reference point a pin needs; can't be caught by the same trick twice) → **Cascade.**
- **CASCADE** ⚖️ [REV v5-jul] (was 🔒; jul08 t365) = spend **100% of remaining coherence** to set the Rule's condition to its **most lethal value** ("one"→"zero"). The Rule's final form, not a generic explosion. **Dishonorable** (a sore loser flipping the board to deny an earned win, at the cost of self-erasure). Subtlest counter: resolve the condition against it *before* it panics into Cascade. Dramatic tell: when an in-betweener goes **still / stops trying to escape**, Cascade is coming.

**Honor code (rooted in nature):** only a **fair, genuinely-uncertain contest** produces rich transition (their food). So they demand **equal duels** (1v1, 2v2, always matched), bind themselves by their own Rules to keep it fair, and **cultivate worthy opponents** — imbuing mortals with Rules and setting them to fight, watching for any mortal worthy of a personal duel. Clean loss = honorable; Cascade = shameful. Jon & Derrek (living transition) = the ultimate coveted opponents.

**Two categories of Rule-bearer** ⚖️ [REV v5-jul] (was 🔒; jul08 t365) (the second was added for the Book-3 protagonist):
- **The AFFLICTED** — a mortal *given* a Rule unasked; can't aim/master it (transition is alien to a Remnant soul — no learning curve, only scarring); pays unpredictable, often harmful costs; can't safely Cascade. Anchored by mortal coherence (blurry/shaken but rarely fully dissolves). Each is a flawed *preview* — a demi-boss implying a true in-betweener "master" who granted the Rule. (Two-stage villain/ally template: the haunted amateur, then the alien master.)
- **The VICTOR** — a mortal who **defeated a threshold being in fair contest** and was *awarded* the Rule as the honorable prize. Because they *won it through understanding*, they can **wield it with intention and skill** (the afflicted cannot). Legendarily rare. *(This is the Book-3 protagonist — see `08_CHARACTERS.md`.)* 🌊 *(v5: the book structure has since changed — Book 1 is now the far future with Derrek's son as hero, and whether that hero carries a Rule is open [t333/t345, t380]; this reference awaits Patrick.)*

### THE MAZE-LAND — a Rule laid on a region (v5) [t146–162]
The same act as a Rule laid on a room, scaled to a chunk of land:
- **It is a place, not a geometric shape** — "hills and land with rivers fish birds etc." [t152]. "Its literally a place where the rule beast laid his condition. Its just a chunk of land" [t154]. The in-betweener made nothing; the land and its life were already there [t154–155].
- **The walls are warped reality:** "Doors you can only pass if you dematerialize and reform on the other side. Long stretches where reality is so heavily warped unless you can compress it around you you'll never pass it in a lifetime" [t150]. Passing it means understanding phase-shifting and decoherence [t150].
- **Whole peoples live inside:** "entire clans and families live in different sections of the maze. Entire empires born in one segment who never leave" [t150].
- **Escape is unremarkable:** those who escape "arent teleported back to earth. They just cross from one seemingly similar field into another and nothing really seems to change however they are now back" [t154].
- **Outsiders wander in** and become stuck — "Try to return home and end up on a looping road that always returns to the castle or whatever" [t156].
- **THE KEEPER (the spider)** [NEW v5-wk: 🌊 naming collision — "keeper" is now also the fractal-level title (wk W35–W36; glossary KEEPER / CONSUMER / BLIGHT); say which is meant] lives at the center: "The biggest castle on the tallest hill right in the center where his void can spread furthest" [t158]. **Bound but not trapped** (the spider and the web, above) [t160]; "He wouldnt leave" [t162] — though he could, by splitting [t164].
- **Known instance:** the in-betweener that took the dwarves sold to it; those who win free are the **Returned (placeholder name)** — race lore in `07_BEINGS.md`. Their powers are **new forms of Remnant magic learned from their environment** (decoherence, phasing, compression), **NOT stolen Rule-magic** — Patrick: "unique powers they learned from their environment not that they somehow learned rule beast magic" [t148]. They fuse enchantment, soul magic and the Void's warping into one craft [t514]. 🌊 The technology they built from what the cage taught them [t146] is unnamed (Claude's working term "Rule-engines" is unratified). [NEW v5-wk] The Returned were also vivisected; they reverse-engineered captured in-betweener trinkets (wk W37).

### KNOWN INSTANCE — the Tower rule-beast 🟡 (story-layer cross-ref; full entry in `09_STRUCTURE.md` / `13_PROSE_AND_SCENES.md`)
Captured by Derrek's rehearsed counter (it believed it was the most powerful being in the room; he had perfected the trap over countless encounters) and bound in its own Void-anchored room [t132–135]; bound there "UNTIL a new foe loses" [t136]. ## Creation generations 🔒 (a SIZE spectrum, not staggered creation — reconciled this session)
> **⚠️ These tiers are fragment-SIZE, not waves of creation.** All races coalesced in the ONE shatter (`03_COSMOLOGY.md`); none were made later. The list below sorts by fragment size (→ body-durability → lifespan → generational distance to the origin), NOT time of creation. "First Coalesced / Latecomers" = *near vs. far from the origin in generational depth*, because big fragments live in long strides and small ones churn through many short lives — same age as peoples, different memory-depth.
1. **Transcendent (largest fragments):** gods. Need no warmth/food, can exist anywhere; some create **pocket dimensions.** *(v5: demons are no longer listed here as a born order — angels/demons are now the far end of the soul-theft continuum, made not born; see Tier 1, t666/t674.)*
2. **Elder Races (large fragments):** **Dragons, Giants, Elves — the three true elders** (v5, t116–t118). Long strides → the beginning is only a few lifetimes back, near and vivid. 🌊 (Door open for more elder races.) **Changelings are no longer a race in this list** — they are elder-*tier* in power but **made, not born**, from any race (t118, t484, t680; see CHANGELINGS).
3. **Latecomers (small fragments):** humans, orcs, dwarves, goblins, gnomes. Short-lived, multiply fast, the origin decayed into dim myth they're too consumed to regard. *(Birth mechanism for ALL races: diffuse unclaimed Remnant channeled into the child at conception — `03_COSMOLOGY.md`.)* (Full builds of the latecomers live in `10_WORLD.md`.) [NEW v5-jul] *(The July gnome build — cheerful bright cities, viewed as weak, self-deceived about their safety, dwarf-sized Remnant, second only to changelings at assassination — and the goblin/troll notes (jul23 t50–t68) belong in `10_WORLD.md`'s GNOMES & GOBLINS section.)*
4. **Scraps (smallest fragments):** beasts, monsters, animals. Low Remnant, still genuine fragments. *(Elementals were demoted out of the giants into this beast/bestiary region — t78, t102 ruling 3 — but their positive definition is **un-ratified**; see 🌊 below and OPEN ITEMS.)*

Two rough roads: large *born* fragments vs. mortals who *learned* deep mastery over time (pure scale of Remnant × skill — no fusion ladder). **Two paths, "physical and psychic" (t670):** *"A god can be a being who perfected gravity magic to harden their body beyond stone, or an em specialist who can twist matter at a whim"* — and, on the psychic side, the soul mages below.

Good/kind ≠ angel and cruel ≠ demon; the line is far more blurred (t674).

### GIANTS — symbolically EARTH — the god-like race

- **Largest bodies → largest Remnant → most POTENT users** (not most skilled — they can *afford* expressions no one else can pay for). 🌊 *(Giants' trained skill: NEEDS_PATRICK, Pass 2026-11 open calls, C-45R.)* **Signature mastery: massive-scale TRUE TRANSMUTATION and will-imposed reshaping** — a giant takes matter and forces it to *become* what it wills, holding the form by sheer will, at scales no one else can pay for (the engine behind raising hills, carving valleys, the monumental architecture, the grand starships). Distinct from dwarves: **dwarves mine → forge → enchant existing matter**; **giants transmute and will matter into being and shape.** They are **powerful, ACTIVE users — never passive landmarks.** 🌊 *(Whether a giant working is "fired and left" or held — see OPEN ITEMS.)*

### ELVES — symbolically WATER — mirror to dragons
- Patient, calm, **ancient but MORTAL** (NOT "near-immortal": they age very slowly and can be killed, but they age and die; Constitution 4a). **Long-lived, but distinctly LESS than giants — and less than dragons** (v5, t272).
