- **The hunger is for everything — want, not need (ruled, t480).** Humans are the race that is never satisfied. Once need is solved, the hunger does not stop, because it was never need that drove them; it was always **want**.
- **Pride — most deadly, never the only [NEW v5-jul] (jul23 t82).** "Humans can still be plagued by pride. Could even be their most deadly sin… without us smooshing it into their only sin." (Per the vice-set rule above: a ranking of tendency, not an assigned sin.)
- **Science and magic were driven by war [NEW v5-jul] (jul08 t93; locked by Claude t94).** "Humans as the central antagonistic force drove science not as curiosity like in our world where military might became an afterthought but instead war was the foregone conclusion of this world. Science and magic grew lockstep in tandem with the ever progressing war of dominance humans waged across the world." "The deep pride in humans is exactly what created a being like Derrek." [NEW v5-wk] **Why humans say "science":** dragons were humanity's **first teachers** — which is why humans call magic "science" (wk W63). Faith, magic and science are one act under different names (wk W57; see RELIGION below).
- **Root = necessity (sympathetic, not chosen) — 🌊 see CONFLICT above:** short lives, endless birth, perpetual scarcity. They *are* always short — on land, food, homes, time. The hunger is real and not evil in itself.
- **Mask = pride / supremacy (the sin):** they can't look at their own endless consuming and call it hunger, so they wrap it in a story of **supremacy** — "we don't take because we're desperate, we take because we're *owed*, because we're highest, because our lord granted us this." Pride is the **alibi for appetite.** Question their need for your land and they don't say "we're starving," they say "how dare you, your betters were granted this." The defensiveness is the tell — pride flares hottest where the need is most naked, because its job is to keep them from seeing the need. **"Generalist" is the symptom, not the identity** — they spread into every domain because they can't bear one they haven't conquered (adaptability as insecurity). **(v5, t488):** the supremacy has a theology — their hunger "was always behind an idea of supremacy born from an idea they are **the true rightfully anointed children of the One**."
- **The one weird specific: FERVENT ZEALOTRY ✅ (ruled, t488).** Humans in this world are **the religious ones.** They **worship Derrek and Jon's patron** (the puppeteer — `03_COSMOLOGY.md`). Derrek **started a cult among the humans as he conquered them, enslaved them, and turned them to his will over time** (t488); he took them **by force and by extreme charisma both** (t552), telling a despised, short-lived people they were the anointed children of the One. *(Per the race-model discipline: conditions, never blood — zealotry is the culture Derrek's rule produced.)* [NEW v5-wk] (How a religion works — portrait of its god, recruitment network of pact champions — see RELIGION below, wk W57.)
- **Parasites — take the gift, deny the giver:** every pillar of human success is borrowed from a longer-lived race that learned to sustain — **elven medicine, giant architecture, dragon law, dwarven refinement** — yet they treat the givers as **tools** (when submissive) or **enemies** (when not), never equals, because equality would mean admitting dependence, which would shatter the pride that hides the need. *(But it's not pure take — it's interpenetration: humans move dwarven gold, guard dragon fortresses, advise giants. The whole web uses the whole web; humans are just the largest, shortest-clocked, most fragmented, most chaotic node.)* *[NEW v5-jul] And it runs both ways (jul08 t93): the other races "know they are successful off the backs of humanity. Same of all races. It is a chaotic and parasitic relationship they all have. Humans' constant need to feed and expand forces the other races into a life or death struggle to keep up or be assimilated into the machine that is humanity."* *[NEW v5-jul] (modern era, jul08 t295)* Take-the-gift-deny-the-giver reaches its end in the modern era: human descendants long after the elves left see elven design **as their own** — told from birth that the cities they live in were built for them by their ancestors, never who really built them.
- **Greatest victims of their own cycle:** the churn eats humans first and worst — more of them, shorter-lived, breeding into scarcity, enslaving and grinding up *each other* (human lords enslave human peasants; human factions grind human armies to dust). They have no shared aim the way an elf-clan or dwarven-hold does, so they turn on themselves hardest of all. The parasite's primary host is itself.
- [NEW v5-cc] ✅ **Numbers, tactics, will.** "Humans understand they cannot match a giant or dragon one on one. They dont like to admit it but they cannot match elves either. They have higher remnant. A human taking your land saying "my children will starve, I'm sorry, you are my equal and I owe you" is tragic-not-damned; one saying "I'm your better, be grateful" is the parasite. Same land taken — the sin is the *story.* Over-index on necessity and slavery gets excused; over-index on pride and they're cartoons. Keep the blade sharp. *(🌊 This bullet leans on the necessity root — see CONFLICT above.)*
- **No monolith (t596):** humans have many factions and powers. ## The long-memory enmity cycle 🔒 (human ↔ elder races)
- The elder races carry **personal, living memory of human atrocities that humans have forgotten** across thousands of buried generations. A dragon or giant grieves the fall of some human empire as a fresh wound (a family it knew, a valley it watched burn) while the humans who'd "owe" for it died out a hundred times over, their descendants living in a bright new civilization built on the literal ashes the elder still mourns. *(v5: dragons are second-longest-lived (t272) — some who lived through the giants' betrayal day still live; giants who survived it remember it personally.)*
- The elder doesn't hate *these* humans — it hates **humanity as a recurring organism**: the same catastrophe rebooting forever with fresh actors who think they're the first, never learning because they never *remember* long enough to learn.
- **The cruel symmetry:** the living human is genuinely innocent of the ancient act, so the hatred reads to him as baffling unearned prejudice — and a proud, needy people who feel hated for no reason they can see answer with **their sin.** Wounded pride demands the hurt be answered; they cast themselves as the aggrieved party and commit the *next* atrocity, believing themselves the victim — writing the fresh wound the elder carries into the next era. **The ancient grievance manufactures the new grievance it's about to earn.** Both sides' worldview is confirmed by the same event; the event is the cycle regenerating itself.
- **Why it's load-bearing for the human sin specifically:** pride cannot receive hatred as *information.* To ask "what did we do?" and take the answer seriously would mean admitting the ancestors earned it → admitting the recurring-organism is real → admitting supremacy is a lie over a wound. Pride forecloses the inquiry that would break the loop. **The sin keeps itself invisible to its owner; the cycle is the sin defending itself.** *(Fractal: the same shape as Jon's loop and Derrek's loop — a being trapped by the exact flaw that prevents it from seeing the trap. Never stated on the page; it makes the text rhyme.)*
- **No clean hands here either:** the elder's justified grief is ALSO an input that produces the next crime (radiating contempt at an innocent until his pride corners him into lashing out), and the elders' withdrawal-into-grudge (bitter dragons, indifferent giants) is its own abdication — they could have shaped humanity and chose contempt. *(v5 clarification, t56: the giants' "indifference" is a surface — it is long since locked that the giants are deeply upset and wage a long **war of attrition**, building the cathedral ships so the dragons will kill one another, `07`.)* Everyone in the loop is victim and cause. *(The elder who finally understands this — sees the hatred as justified-but-futile, the human as innocent, his own withdrawal as complicity — is exactly the giant-who-spanned-three-eras mentor figure, `07_BEINGS.md`; in the far future, [REV v5-cc] a kindly giant who tells the hero the true history ("the last friendly giant" as a special figure is retired — BANK 11-07; cc R116) (was: "the kindly **last friendly giant**"), t334, `08`. The elder who broke the grudge.)*

## ORCS — humanity's pattern with the mask OFF (greed their MOST COMMON expression, never an assigned sin) 🔒
*[REV v5-jul] header (was: "ORCS — sin: GREED (humanity's sin with the mask OFF)") — sin decoupled as a racial attribute (jul23 t52; header wording per the t75 write). The orcs' nature lines below stay locked; only the single-sin label is retired.*
- **Root = the most ACUTE form of the human wound:** shortest-lived of all peoples, most overcrowded, fastest clock — **the clock steals the future and CHEAPENS the past**: a horizon so close the future is almost meaningless, and deep history *unimportant to the race as a whole* (`03` generational-depth at its extreme — the origin and old eras thin to dim myth; too consumed by the present to look back). **Priority, not incapacity (corrected):** individuals remember their own lives perfectly well; the rare scholars record (selectively); **occult leaders pass the traditions orally**, as oral cultures always have. The race keeps a short ledger by disposition, never by defect. Their greed isn't a defect; it's **desperation at a clock where "later" barely exists,** so grabbing now is the only rational move. (Same wound as humans, more extreme.)
- **Humanity's program run nakedly:** they mirrored the human extract-and-dominate structure (weren't long-lived enough to build broad governance, or given the intelligence-slack/charisma to launder greed into legitimacy — **conditions producing the outcome, NEVER innate deficiency**; they're short-horizoned, not stupid). So they run the same game humans do, but with **no mask that works** — no honor-story that convinces, no charm that buys forgiveness. **They show openly what the respectable races do in disguise, and are hated for it.**
- **Subjugated for DEFIANCE, not weakness:** offered the subordinate place in the hierarchy, they **refused to align** — kept resisting a game they couldn't win, burned every bridge, destroyed all good will through repeated collisions, until mutual contempt hardened into wholesale enslavement. Defiance punished, not pity exploited. [NEW v5-jul] In Patrick's formulation (jul08 t185): **refusing to accept being less, they were forced to be less.** *(He framed it there as orcs having "earned their subjugation"; the later July build ruled "they earned it" purely the world's lie — see below — so only the refused-less/forced-less shape is carried.)* The other races enslave them and feel no contradiction, because by their own supremacist logic orcs "fail in every metric" and deserve the bottom — **that verdict is the enslavers' self-justification, NEVER the author's truth.**
- **THE OLDEST CHAINS 🔒 (the three-masters arc):** orcs were **born into bondage when time was new — under the giants' forced protection** (enslavement by several measures of the word, though the gentlest it would ever be: love led the giants' hand — as it did for ALL races under them [REV v5-verify] *(the elves excepted: they always fell outside giant control, jul08 t225 — matching `07`'s retirement of the unqualified "ALL races")*). They **fought in the dragons' coalition** 🌊 *(Claude's reading, not Patrick's: drawn in once the capital was dead. Patrick ruled only one event, not coordinated entirely by dragons, a few warned (cc R091); whether and how orcs were drawn in is open — `NEEDS_PATRICK` L37)* believing the manufactured promise — *freedom as equals* — and were **re-chained by the dragons immediately**, under masters more ruthless and vile than the ones they'd bled to escape (`07` Darkest Age). When dragons receded and humans rose, they **refused the offered lesser place** (the defiance above) and were subjugated a third time — by the race that takes from all others. **They never truly freed themselves; every "liberation" was a promise betrayed.** In the orcs' experience each master was worse than the last — and each a **different KIND of chain**: forced protection (love-led), then instrumental control (aimed at dragon ends), then parasitic consumption (expand and use) — *the sin-map experienced sequentially from underneath (derived: the three masters' recorded masks, felt as three bondages)* — and "they earned it" is **purely the world's lie**, one more excuse the awful people of this world use to justify enslaving fragments of the One. Their own enslaving of "lesser" races (goblins, trolls, others) is **trauma-replication, not invention**: they dominated because chains were all they had ever known — not because memory fails, but because **there was never anything else to remember**: three masters all the way back (per the chain, no self-won freedom ever existed to record). **They live in complete ignorance of any life other than slavery** — so when freedom briefly touched them, the only mechanism of power their memory could supply was the one that had always been used on them. *(Derived, corrected: the inversion of the long-memory enmity cycle — the race that suffered LONGEST keeps the SHORTEST account of it. Each orc remembers their own lifetime's wounds vividly; it is the deep ledger of the eras that thins to myth — by disinterest and the trauma-thin archive, never incapacity.)*
- **Grievance without archive 🔒:** ignorance of history is NOT absence of grievance. Orcs carry a **cultural understanding that they were wronged** — an inherited *shape* of resentment that fuels their anger and defiance — without the content: each orc remembers only what was done **in their own lifetime.** The wound transmits; the history doesn't. They know they were wronged the way you know a bruise — by the ache, not the blow. (This is the fuel of the recorded defiance.)

- **The orc scholars — victimhood as total explanation 🔒 (their self-deception, completing the symmetry):** the few orcs who learn history learn it **warped through the permanent-victim lens**: orcs taught as *the tools of power*, their slavery framed as **the critical reason the other races succeeded** — the hidden engine of everyone else's prosperity. Partially true (orc labor genuinely underpins the machine) and fundamentally wrong: they **cannot comprehend that everyone is victim to the same authorless cycle** (the churn, above) — that what orcs actually lost was *the same game every race played*, lost through **lower competency at it** (no working mask, no clock for institutions, no charisma to launder the grab). The scholars promote a real loss into a cosmic conspiracy, because "we played the same game and lost" is unbearable. **And the archive itself guarantees it:** orcs barely bother recording history at all — what moved the rare scholar to write was **catastrophe**, their own lifetime's great tragedies. So the orc historical corpus is **trauma-selected at the source**: not a neutral record read through a victim lens — **the corpus IS the lens, materialized.** Only tragedy ever got written, because only tragedy made anyone write; an honest scholar working from that archive still concludes the orcs' whole story is suffering. **Forever slaves in mind and body:** the victimhood-cosmology doesn't merely misexplain — it **licenses perpetration**: if orcs are the eternal wronged, nothing orcs do can be the same wrong — so in freedom's brief windows they repeated the exact cycle they constantly complain was applied to them, whip in hand, grievance on tongue, no contradiction perceived. The body's chains are the world's; the mind's are their own.
- **"HATE" — the bruise, named 🔒:** the orcs' own word for the inherited ache is **hate.** Other races, watching, would call what orcs carry *loathing, despising* — true disgust and wholesale condemnation — and that outside reading **adds to the cage**: a people perceived as made of spite justifies every tightened grip. **Their culture itself IS hate** — even granted the impossible (the capacity to see other races as equals), the culture would remain: **every orc action, read through the lens of hate, makes sense.** Hatred for **each other** (the recorded infighting), for **others**, and for **the very past itself** (the trauma-corpus). All orc existence is led from rage, hatred, and **entitlement** — the victim-cosmology's yield: the wronged are *owed.* *(Derived, corrected: hate is the CHEAPEST inheritance — it needs no archive, it rides the ache, and every generation renews it from fresh wounds. Traditions and rites DO pass orally through the occult leaders; the deep past thins to myth — so what arrives intact across generations is the wound and the rites. The culture is hate not because nothing else can be inherited, but because hate inherits itself. And from inside, their greed has no name — it isn't greed to them, it's **restitution**: taking what the wronged are owed.)* **The ratchet:** their greed and foresightlessness destroy their own prospects and close the others' hand ever tighter — and under that grip the hate slowly warps into **complete contempt.** The cage finishes itself from the inside.
- **Ritual magic & the demon-commune — the orcs' magical culture 🔒:** orcs **resonate with pact-work** — ritual magics, blood-rites, communing with demons are their characteristic magical lean (a resonance, NEVER a title: no race is THE anything — pacts are practiced across the whole world per `06`; orcs simply lean hardest on this road, for the reason below). **Mechanism, not essence** (Law 8 — cultural tradition, never a magic-lock; individual orcs vary): orcs are the weakest-in-magic major race, and Pacts are canonically **the equalizer** (`06` — a deal lets a weak being punch far above its Remnant). So the magically poorest people naturally lean hardest on *borrowed* power: **pact-craft is the most open magical road the world left them** — not the only one (Law 8: individuals vary; some orcs work Remnant like anyone), but the one their condition made most rewarding, most taught, most common. The races read the rites as final proof of savagery — *they treat with demons; they were never people* — one more entry in the "earned it" lie, and among the most potent. The hypocrisy is recorded canon: per `06`, god-blessings, blood rituals, and demon-deals are **all Pacts — one system, differing only by patron and price.** A human blessed by a god and an orc bargaining with a demon perform the same act; the world sanctifies one patron and demonizes the other. **Orc "occultism" is everyone's religion with a poorer patron.** (Double-faced, per the build: from outside, devil-worship; from inside, the only magic available.) **This answers the Orc King's HOW** (`08`): his demon pact is not an individual anomaly — it is the apex expression of his people's one magical tradition. **This is the orc mask over the orc wound** — every race warps its condition into a story that protects it from self-knowledge, even at the bottom of the hierarchy, even in chains. (Boundary, held: the scholars' cosmology is false; the wrong done to orcs is still REAL — this does not resurrect "they earned it," which remains purely the world's lie. The scholars teach a true grievance inside a false cosmology — arming the rage while blinding it.)

## ELVES — the EXCEPTION that proves the rule 🔒
- **The one race the human machine could never dissolve.** Since the beginning they cohered on their own terms, created their own works, and maintained **deliberate autonomy from the human machine** (functioning relationships with the other races, yes — but never woven-in, never dependent, never assimilated). While human society is filled with and codependent on the other races, the elves stand apart.
- **Why it works (not special pleading — it's the bond, `07_BEINGS.md`):** humanity's whole method is worm-in-and-absorb-from-within, one separable individual at a time. The bond **rejects the foreign "I" like tissue rejects a graft** — so the elves are the one substance the machine structurally cannot dissolve. They don't resist by willpower; they're un-absorbable by nature. *(v5: the one deliberate crack is the **bond-spoof chip** — a device that lets a wearer pass as an elf; July canon approved for banking at t630; details `06`/`07`.)* *[NEW v5-jul] "The chip is the deliberate vehicle to deliver chaos and conflict to the elves at a scale they never before experienced" (jul23 t150). Before it, changelings categorically cannot infiltrate elves; with it, the elves are suddenly vulnerable to the group they had hunted forever (jul23 t161 pt 12, confirmed t162).*
- **The cosmological pole:** where humans are the One's **shatter** at its most chaotic (a million appetites cohering into nothing), the elves are the closest thing left to the One **un-shattered** (many who are functionally one — surviving unity). The two races are the two poles of the whole cosmology; their conflict carries the reunion/dissolution duality (`03_COSMOLOGY.md`). [NEW v5-wk] *(Read as theme, not strict cosmic halves: the axis has a neutral middle; duality = the name versus the act — wk W29.)*
- **The oldest war:** [RESTORED v5-verify] *This earns the exodus: Jon didn't **convince** a peaceful people to fear a new enemy —* the elves have stood against human domination since the dawn; they were already fighting the long cold war. It wasn't a new war — it was the oldest one reaching its climax.

## DWARVES — independence at all costs; greed as its learned strategy (never a trait, never an assigned sin) 🔒
*[REV v5-jul] header (was: "DWARVES — hunger: GREED (neutrality is its learned strategy, never a trait)") — jul23 t52/t54; header wording per the t75 write ("greed as learned strategy, never a trait, and never an assigned sin") with Patrick's independence root.*
- **The root is INDEPENDENCE; greed is its strategy [REV v5-jul] (jul23 t54)** *(was: "The hunger is GREED")*. "Dwarves can tend towards greed because their culture values **independence at all costs** and they weighed that being the arms dealer and being rich was a great way to stay independent — but not just a flat boring all dwarves are greedy." **Grimdark, not noble partnership.** Dwarves are not honest brokers by nature; they are the **indiscriminate merchant**: a people who discovered that greed is *maximally satiated by having no friends.* Sell weapons to your ally's enemy — unacceptable betrayal. Sell weapons to both sides as a neutral party — completely fine, just business. **Neutrality is NOT a core trait, a value, or a personality** (🚫 tripwire: do not encode "dwarves are neutral" as nature) — it is the **learned, world-forged optimal strategy** for greed: they watched the societal lessons of this world (thrones fall; sides lose) and converged on the position that lets them sell to everyone forever. Behavior forged by the world, never innate — same discipline as every race. *(Precision, t148: neutral doesn't mean "at the behest of neutrality" — they **earned and bought** neutrality by being too costly to conquer.)*
- **The Switzerland metaphor:** the mountain people, trading gold, gems, and precision craft for a **promise of armed neutrality.** Their fortresses reflect their nature — built toward perfection, magically infused (impossible materials, incredibly precise math, marvelous works — their craft **based on giant craft**, learned in the giants' age). Too costly to assault, too useful to destroy. [NEW v5-jul] **The dwarven mini-age (jul08 t167):** "They based their work on giant craft. They helped the giants in their own age which was the Dwarven mini age." **Indispensable, not inconquerable (jul08 t299):** "Dwarves made their craft super specific to make themselves indispensable not inconquerable. The loss of dwarven engineering wasnt a cost analysis any race wanted to make… The dwarves still somewhat relied on the other races. Elves held firmly apart."
- **The family face ✅ (ruled, t590–t594).** Dwarves present as **a rowdy, loud, aggressive, extremely loyal, extremely caring family unit — ruthless to anyone outside**: caring only for the family at the expense of the other. Their family trees are **rigid and hierarchical**; they don't swerve much. **But family is not their golden law:** for all the talk of family first, **they sold family to the in-betweener to avoid enslavement themselves** (the Sale, `07`). What governs them is not one great law but **a sophisticated series of laws**, as the modern world has. 🌊 *Claude's gloss "family is what they love, continuity is what they actually serve" (t595) — not individually confirmed; flagged.*
- **Government: bureaucratic autocracy ✅ (ruled, t594/t596).** A **highly bureaucratic autocracy**: a few **emperors** of their own dwarven empires, with **councils and boards** and a **very heavy tie to the businesses.** There are **several emperors, each running his own empire of the dwarves** — no monolith (t596).
- **The trade empire abroad ⚖️ (t146; banked at t203).** At home the holds; abroad, the dwarves run **a genuine commerce empire** — the trading-company model (Patrick's touchstone, t146: "Like the Dutch east indies" — the trading-company model; 🌊 real-world comparison kept for Patrick to rule): monopolies, private armies, merciless commerce. **Neutral in wars, ruthless in trade.** An extension of armed neutrality, not a change to it.
- **A district in every city — shown, never told [NEW v5-jul] (jul08 t223/t225).** Dwarves keep a district in every race's towns — the elven city included. In the human city the reader notices dwarves but no elves, just as there are no humans in the elven city; "you'll see that dwarves work with both without having to tell everyone." "It's a fact they sell to everyone. You dont have to tell the reader that." (Craft rule → `13`.)
- **The chip's price (far future) [NEW v5-jul] (jul23 t154/t156/t158).** Dwarves "who only care for money and the precision of their craft would hold no qualms about dissecting and studying live and dead elves in a variety of sick ways to design and perfect their chip" — elves bought as captives from far-distant wars, through a human company that specializes in slavery (background logic only; no named institution). [NEW v5-wk] That slaver company is the **supply chain of the organ trade** (wk W67; see ORGAN TRADE below). [REV v5-wk2: 🌊 proposed, unconfirmed — Claude's suggestion (chat t348), never taken up by Patrick] *(Maker refined toward the Returned faction by the t629 list approved at t630 — implied, never stated; and July's "partway through Book 3" timing uses the old numbering — both 🌊 for Patrick. Chip mechanics → `06`.)*
- **They use the weaker — including dwarves (t566).** Dwarves don't think of the world as a ladder of races, but in practice they use those less powerful than themselves, **other dwarves included.** **Gnomes are their natural servants — likely where the majority of gnomes live** (t566); by the far future, gnomes are the dwarves' **indentured class, sold to whoever wants one** (t568). *(🌊 t566 as written also says "elves" — flagged as a probable slip; not written as canon.)*
- **The missing party in every crisis (far future, t538).** Dwarves build the **drives** humans and others travel with, the **focusing chambers** dragon ships fight with (t50, t220), and the chambers feeding the giants' forges; their sold-off kin, the Returned, drive the worst of it (t146). **They profit from all three crises — neutral in every war, selling to every side.** They are "the dwarven slavers" of Patrick's far-future list (t334); the giants' mass-buying of lifeforms runs through **dwarven suppliers** (t278). [NEW v5-wk] **Dwarven traffickers** carry the Inquisition's secret sale of captured dark elves to rich humans (wk W68).

Also yes humans would also have members studying dwarven tech the way some gravitate to dragon magic" (Patrick, BANK 11-16 [DWARVES]) (cc R052, R053). *(Land, neutrality and how far they bent to dragons wait on C-56.)*
- **The mirror pair: dwarves and changelings ✅ (ruled, t540).** **"Dwarves hold no official offices and yet stay indispensable from all parties. Changelings exist inside all parties and yet are in fact useless and completely parasitic."** (Changeling side → `07`.) [REV v5-wk] *(Patrick's t540 wording kept; read "inside all parties" under wk W19 — changelings are now largely monsters, only a few clever ones at court.)*
- **The second unsubjugated race — by the OPPOSITE mechanism from the elves.** Elves stayed free by *separation* (un-assimilable, withdrawn, no trading or mingling). Dwarves stayed free by **entanglement so deep they cannot be removed** — embedded literally into the bedrock, and economically into every society (found throughout human cities *while also* holding their own kingdoms, peasants, kings, land, resources, and wars). Humanity never subjected them — not that humans would find it easy (`09`: the "indispensable ally"; computing knowledge had to be *coerced*, not conquered — `07`). *(Precision held, t144–t146: the **people** were never subjugated; a **group** of dwarves was — sold by their own to an in-betweener. See the Returned, below and `07`.)*
- **The empire that never fell 🔒 (precision matters):** many races have held complete civilizations — the dwarven distinction is **unbroken continuity.** Humans' empire is the newest (no claim to longevity); giants lost their thrones to dragons; dragons receded before humans' rise. **Dwarves and elves alone never fell** — never waned into ruin, never lost their empire. Bad years, deep declines, yes — but as **managed plateau**: dips and reclimbs, constant over time, never rise-and-fall. They never ruled the world (no numbers, no elder-tier Remnant, no elder lifespan — they can't win any classic domain), so they never entered the apex-fall pattern (`07` Darkest Age: giants→dragons→humans) — and are therefore, with the elves, outside it entirely: **the truest, longest-lasting empire, forged by never reaching for the throne.** 🌊 *CONFLICT — for Patrick: "several emperors, each with his own empire" (t596) vs. the single unbroken empire. Claude's reading (t597: the dwarven order never collapses while individual empires rise, merge and decline) was not objected to but never confirmed. The elves' exodus from Earth (t452) may also bear on "elves never fell."*
- **Temperament:** patient but temperamental — they will spend long hours forging a blade, and when they need to shove it inside you, their emotions run **very hot.** (Cultural disposition per Law 8, never a lock; and distinct from orc greed — the orcs' is desperation at a short clock, failing nakedly; dwarven greed is patient, institutionalized, and *succeeding* behind the merchant's counter. [REV v5-jul] Same tendency, opposite fortunes — *was: "Same sin, opposite fortunes"; the shared-root-sin framing was dropped with the decoupling, jul23 t51–t52.*)
- **The schism (factions):** **Integrationists** — the other races are profitable, useful allies; these dwarves haven't yet been completely revolted by outsiders' behaviors — vs. **Isolationists** — dwarves need no outside aid, and accepting it only fragments and weakens dwarven power; a conglomerate of genuine racists *and* the legitimately disillusioned (no clean hands in either camp). And a third people beside them: **the Returned** (below).
- **The Returned and their kin ✅ (ruled, t620–t624; placeholder name).** The Returned (dwarves sold to an in-betweener's maze-prison, escaping one at a time — full build `07`) are **taught** that they were sold. They resent a status so low they were sold off so easily, and their servitude — but they also understand the maze gave them new powers, and are **grateful** for that. When one wins the maze they are simply released — free now. Some **return to dwarven holds and beg for jobs and placement**; some bring a kind of dowry earned inside to buy property; some become **bandits.** Ordinary dwarves see them as **distant relatives** — "hey mate, you were the bottom of the ledger, you'd have done the same," and a grumble of agreement. They weren't criminals the way the dark elves were, so **there is no reason to hunt them or discriminate.** The maze turned them from a people concerned only with money into a people **consumed by the drive never to be bound again** — coin over most things, and now absolute freedom too, so they are absolutely unscrupulous (t624).
- **The Darkest Age stance ✅ (resolved):** dwarves were **uninvolved in the coup except as arms-suppliers — to BOTH sides, even then.** The neutrality doctrine wasn't born from the giants' fall; it was *already operating* in the world's oldest war — the most consistent race, staunch and rule-based, running the same strategy since the deepest era (their one-weird-specific: **consistency itself** — the people who never change course). This is why the giants' shared grudge (`07`) does not fall on them the way it falls on the complicit: predictable, rule-bound commerce with all parties is categorically different from [REV v5-cc] the knife of those who rose (cc R091) (was: "the coalition's knife") — and why the far-future giant/dwarf partnership (`07`) carries no contradiction.
- **The one somewhat-happy story 🔒:** the dwarves are the race that **thrived most of all** — complete unwavering neutrality let them prosper while every throne rose and fell. (Caveat held: *individual* dwarves have suffered greatly, often; it is the *people* whose line never broke. And grimdark structurally needs one race that thrived — the control group that proves the world's brutality is a choice-space, not a law.)
- **Dwarven FTL (far future, t438):** a **dimensional squeeze** warp drive.
- 🌊 **Open:** whether the dwarven mini-age (their golden age inside the giants' era — its existence stated, jul08 t167) has a named loss at all, given no great fall; formally lock master-enchanter status (`06` — one word from locked; the Returned's "natural skill at enchantment" is noted at t514); dwarven faith, the bottom of dwarven society, daily life (t560/t631).

## GNOMES & GOBLINS — the small races (v5) ⚖️ position / ✅ nature as stated
- **Gnomes.** Latecomer race. **(medieval era)** kind of happy; seen as the most lowly because they don't play politics; **power users** (t284). Happy gnome villages are a **medieval-era image only** — remote forest towns, likely gone by the end (t568). **(far future)** an **indentured class of the dwarves**, sold to whoever wants one (t568). The race viewed as weakest has one of the strongest representatives at the end — a gnome who became a changeling (t772; `07`/`08`), whose opening act — a ritual learned on his brother, then **enslaving his entire village** — "could be considered one of the worst acts ever committed against gnomes" (t778).
  - **[NEW v5-jul] The gnome build (jul23 t50–t62; Patrick's own).** The **lesser race counter to dwarves**, as humans and orcs parallel each other: "a race who also sort of embodies similar traits done differently" (t50). **Funny and cheerful** — they stand in bleak contrast to the world's grimdark; a gnomish town is "bright and smells good, loud and happy people bustling" (t60). They "care so little of wealth or who claims to be 'boss' that they exist fully there in the moment enjoying life." **Misconception:** their happiness and perceived compliance get them viewed as weak, naive to the brutal realities of the world. **Schism:** those who agree with the outside world that gnomes are too kind, soft and passive and wish to fight for their rights and independence, vs. those content with exactly how things are, unwilling to upset the delicate balance. **No golden age** — "they do fine. They are securely an average race." **Remnant:** a culture valuing education and free thinking gives good Remnant control, and a **Remnant similar in size to a dwarf's** — high-tier scaled-up magic (the "power users" above). With their small stature they are **second only to changelings at things like assassination.** **Self-deception (t62):** "They think they are safe, that's why they are so happy" — they believe their passivity buys peace and protection, blind to the fact that **they aren't sovereign**: they hold their homes only because no one sees them as a threat. [NEW v5-cc] ✅ *No clash with "Noone is just tolerated" (BANK 11-16): their sense of safety is their self-deception, and their villages are gone by the end — tolerance fails, which proves his rule (cc R142).* "Dwarves literally bought their immunity with gold and weapons. Gnomes live in a fragile balance that can be easily upturned at any point." *(Physics-chat scale wins: the happy settlements are the few small remote medieval villages, likely gone by the end, and most gnomes live under the dwarves — t566/t568. July's "gnomish city" wording is carried only as those villages' texture.)*
- **Goblins.** Orcs' own underclass (above) — scarred until they read as animals, yet metaphysically equal, just weaker (jul23 t66–t68). [NEW v5-jul] **The reader will never see a goblin city or a troll fortress** — "their history was destroyed so long ago there's no history left to remember" (jul23 t64). **(far future)** the galaxy doesn't name them separately — **a goblin is just a small orc**, and it is all called "orcs" (t566).

Giant-made cathedral ships are **rare** even with slave-forging, so **dragons have home-brew ships** (t444). (Dragon detail → `07`.)

> # 🟡 STORY LAYER — FLUID / WORK-IN-PROGRESS
> **Nothing in this file is fixed.** Every character, name, plot point, book structure, and scene here is *provisional exploration* — current thinking, not canon. Names are placeholders (Jon, Derrek, the elf, etc. are ALL placeholders). Beats and roles move freely as the story develops. **No 🟡 LAW stamps apply to story content** — only the WORLD/SYSTEM files (Constitution, Glossary, Cosmology, Magic Substrate, External Powers, Beings-categories, Method, Property Inventory) are rigid. Story rests *on top* of that bedrock and stays flexible by design, so new ideas can reshape it without breaking anything. The ONLY hard constraint on story is that it must not violate the WORLD/SYSTEM bedrock (e.g. a scene cannot have someone hurl fusion across a room — that breaks Strong-force physics). Story-vs-story "conflicts" are NOT conflicts; they are just the story being unfinished.

# 12 — METHOD (How We Work)

Process-level items only: no forced triads / no formula (W29, W32, W33), soul-sensing on the page (W09), madness as subtext (W70), no clinical labels (W44/W66 notes), scenes float (W52). New lines `[NEW v5-wk]`; no new 🔒 (report: `changes/B_world_wk.md`).

No new 🔒 (log: `changes/FIX_wk2.md`).

The design discipline behind the whole project. These are 🔒 LAWs about *process* — they protect the work's quality and were hard-won (mostly by the author correcting Claude's reflexes).

---

## The No-Formula / Multi-Scale Law 🔒
- Characters are **not computed** from their positions (no x+y=z).
- Every scale (morality, temperament, favored expressions, loves, duties, …) is **independent, full-range** (with a real middle and a real neutral), and does **NOT** blend into "types" or "corners."
- **Most beings rest in the soft middle of most scales;** the poles are rare. Nobody lives in a corner. ("Dark" is a *tendency that slides by degree in context*, never a category that makes all your acts evil — the cartoon-villain failure mode.)
- Depth lives in the **subtle, often non-aligned** positions a person holds at once — including genuinely **contradictory** ones held whole (Lirael: love AND grief AND duty-above-feeling AND desire, none reconciled; she acts from duty *while* loving). **Stop computing characters; hold their contradictions.**
- The cosmic poles are **bare directions only.** Any meaning/feeling/morality (belonging vs. suffocation, liberty vs. isolation) is *individual*, never definitional. Never assign a pole a tidy thematic value.
- **Don't flatten blurred lines (v5, t674).** Turning a blur into a ladder, a graduation, or a good/bad split is the same failure. The author, correcting Claude on angels/demons/changelings/gods: "Your giving it to much flattening... The line is far more blurred." (Constitution Laws 3, 16.)
- [NEW v5-jul] **Grading scales, not fixed points.** A race or group is never one block that acts all at once: "Duality friend. Duality. Grading scales not a single fixed point" (jul08 t269, on dragons retreating one by one). The world-law form is "Noone is a monolith" (t596; `10_WORLD.md`).
- [NEW v5-jul] **No group is THE anything.** "We've explicitly worked at every step not to make any group THE anything. They simply resonate with pacts" (jul08 t212). Any line that reads "X are the world's Y" should trip the same alarm as "fire user."
- [NEW v5-jul] **Don't harden a tendency into a condition.** Claude's recurring slide: lean → title, strategy → trait, unimportant → impossible. "At 0 point did I say that… I only said due to their short life history is unimportant to them as a whole" (jul08 t213–214). Check the tendency-versus-condition line hardest.
- [NEW v5-jul] **Sins are not racial attributes.** "Lets drop this sin as a racial attribute as per our no locked identities. All races in this world are greedy prideful jealous beings… I think we can do the same thing weve done with every other scale we tried to force" (jul23 t52–54). A sin is "a complex web of interconnected behaviors and motives"; a race's culture and history shape *how* the vices surface (e.g. dwarves value independence at all costs, and arms-dealing wealth serves it — jul23 t54). A vice can be a race's *most deadly* without being its only one (humans and pride, jul23 t82).
- [NEW v5-wk] **No forced triads.** "I dont need to make every trope arbitrarily 3" (wk W33). Don't pad a set to three (or any tidy count) for symmetry.
- [NEW v5-wk] **No formula from method to nature.** The author corrected Claude: there is **no formula** tying god vs. demon to method of ascent — behavior is individual (wk W32). Likewise duality is **not** strict cosmic halves; it is the name versus the act, and the axis keeps a neutral middle (wk W29). Same failure as the grid: a tidy mapping where the author holds a blur.
- **Tell that I'm violating this:** if I start enumerating "the four combinations are…" or drawing a grid, stop.

## Rigor on the substrate; silence on the soul 🔒
Two modes, and using the wrong one is destructive:
- **Substrate (the system: Remnant, the soul-substrate, costs, interactions, and the force/element flavor vocabulary):** be the rigorous engineer **of internal consistency.** Press for hard rules, hunt contradictions against our own canon, demand consistency. **Never audit real-world physics and never do math** — physics is flavor (see "Physics is flavor" below; Constitution 0a).
- **Soul (who a person is and how they therefore express magic):** build the **space of possibility** and then **go quiet.** Never populate it with types. The system must stay *almost arrogantly silent about who people are* — it defines the substrate and stops; the people are sovereign over how they meet it.
- **Why:** the moment a system encodes "this kind of person gets this kind of power," it quantizes individuality and caps versatility. The deepest-character systems keep the rules on the *physics* side of the line and the people on the *character* side. Every "no racial/temperamental lock," "morality is independent," etc. is this line being held.

## Physics is flavor — no audits, no math 🔒 (v5 — re-confirmed by the author; the 🔒 restates locked Constitution 0a)
- Physics is here for the author's **intuition only** — "not laws applied as requirements" (t0–5). Real science is a well of texture to draw from; it never gates a scene (Constitution 0a; `14_PHYSICS_REFERENCE.md` is a non-binding palette).
- **No math.** "Your doing math and we agreed no math" (t72). No numeric size tiers, stat charts, mass or energy budgets, or structural-physics mechanisms (e.g. square-cube auditing). The world owes no physics mechanism for what it does.
- If a physics idea would break the physics/consciousness wall (Constitution 0b/0c), the wall wins — flag it rather than bend it (t6–7).

## Build laws, not a spell list 🔒
- We build **the laws the spells must obey**, never a lookup table of techniques. A spell list pre-solves every fight (characters become loadouts; prose narrates a calculation — dead).
- Test for anything proposed: *"Is this a law the world obeys, or a catalog of outcomes?"* A law *generates* infinite moments; a catalog *forecloses* them ("here are the six gravity techniques, ranked").
- **Characters' specific powers emerge from the story** and are explained *after* (as Lirael's Collapse was recognized, then built on). In a live moment (e.g. Jon vs. an inversion-tornado) we ask: what is it made of? its traits? relative power here? what can the defender perceive? what do they reach for? — invented in the moment, grounded in the laws, never pulled from a menu.
- The groundedness in the **laws** is exactly what *earns* total improvisational **freedom** on top. Freedom above, bedrock below.
- **New powers must not break rarity (v5, t84).** A rare feat stays rare by its cost or its setup (the dragon's once-made stone: "the rock is how we kept it rare").

## The skeleton & build order 🔒 (REWORKED — the rigorous engine was retired)
The original six-joint Sanderson-mirrored build (SOURCE → ACCESS → UNITS → PROGRESSION gates → COST/LIMIT → INTERACTION) was scaffolding for a **rigorous physics-engine magic system that the author deliberately abandoned** for **science-flavored, scene-first, loose magic** (`04_MAGIC_SUBSTRATE.md`). So:
- **Kept & solid:** SOURCE (the One → Remnant; Spirit = active Remnant magic), ACCESS (the awakening gradient; Remnant ceiling), UNITS (principle-work + reproducible spells).
- **Retired as pending bones:** PROGRESSION gates, COST/LIMIT charts, INTERACTION laws — these were the rigorous-engine homework. The only standing limits are **Remnant + skill + fatigue**, and all specifics are **discovered per scene**, never charted.
- **Sanderson's Laws still make a fine QC lens** (understand-it-for-earned-solutions; limitations > powers; deepen-before-expanding) — but as *taste*, not a build checklist.
- *(History, v5 t324: the earliest system — "the 4 elements and 4 forces and 4 alignments as a weird compass" — forced rigid classes and taught what doesn't work. "Me and you did our best work when we made radical changes.")*

## Magic is expression, not derivation 🔒 (the "silence on the soul" line, applied to magic)
Build the **person** completely first (motives, wounds, history, who taught them, what they'd take to); **then** their magic follows as an expression of that person, with the force/element flavor named *last* to describe the output. **No equation in either direction** — not ability→character, not character→ability, not race→element. There are **no force/element "users" or types**, only beings who do magic. This is the same discipline as "rigor on the substrate; silence on the soul" above — now the system stays silent even about *abilities* having an identity, let alone people.
- **Every character is "just a skilled user" (v5).** "As with all our characters she is just a skilled user" (t612) — gravity was the *image* of a move (Lirael's Collapse), never a type. Labels that name a person by a force are retired for the same reason: "Calling him sf straps him of the mastery and dedication it took and awards it to a special category he belongs to" (t136).

## Stability-tier discipline 🔒
- Tag everything 🔒 LAW / ⚖️ FLEXIBLE / 🌊 FLUID (default 🌊; ask when unsure). Mark dead ideas 🚫 RETIRED as tripwires. Story files carry the 🟡 STORY banner ("fluid / work-in-progress") and **never** carry 🔒 — the two-layer rule: rigid WORLD/SYSTEM bedrock vs. fluid STORY (tiers run LAW → FLEXIBLE → FLUID → STORY → RETIRED).
- **Never stamp unconfirmed mechanics with a law-tier marker** (a known recurring error). Claude-proposed or unanswered material goes to FLAGGED_ADDITIONS, not into a file as canon.
- [NEW v5-jul] **Mechanics another model built from the author's general descriptions are adjustable foundations (⚖️), not fixed law.** On Claude Code's rule-beast mechanics: "unfixing and the hold seem like him making mechanics out of my general descriptions… they sound good and can always be adjusted later for scenes" (jul08 t365).
- **Keep every existing marker** when editing; move overturned lines to RETIRED with a reason — never delete silently.
- When something changes, **update it in the one file it lives in**, hunt down downstream references, and leave a RETIRED note where confusion could recur. Never leave stale next to current unflagged. (This is *record, not memory* — read the file before working in its domain.)

Dont stray from what we decide").

## Drafting story and scenes (v5-jul)

[NEW v5-jul] Don't under-rate a race's power either: "Elves were NEVER the underdog or weak" (jul08 t299); "Dont mistake their preferred method of subterfuge as a lack of raw magical ability" (changelings, jul08 t139). - [NEW v5-jul] **What the codex is for.** Mainly laws, ways of interacting, policy positions, racial traits and hierarchy — "the entire architectural guide," "rule Bibles rather than just writing story," able to scale to many stories, games and D&D-like play (jul23 t192); the trilogy may be "just entry one in a ongoing and evolving series" (jul23 t194). - **How the author builds:** he looks at the world and lets an idea morph until it finds its shape (t570); he sees the whole blurry shape first, then refines it (t572).
- **The purpose is the author's own fun.** "My purpose of it is primarily for me. Just for me to have fun"; building the world without finishing storylines is fine (t578–580). Don't push toward finishing a book.
- **Canon governance.** Fixed points bind only official or contributed work; other people's tables can borrow the world and make it their own (t582–587).

## PART ONE — CRAFT

## Craft principle: the numbers are scaffolding, never on the page 🟡
The Remnant/skill/fatigue mechanics are our *engineering tool* for adjudicating what's possible. The reader must only feel the **result** — that one fighter is deep/patient, another fast/hot — never the math. NEVER write "her two parts Earth," "my fire 6," etc. (And per the rework there are no force/element "types" to write anyway — describe the *act*, named in flavor after the fact.) Physics is flavor only — "forces as flavor, not law"; no math, no auditing (t0–5, t72).
- **No character has a "type."** Every character is "just a skilled user" (t612 — Patrick stopped Claude calling the dark-elf heroine a "gravity" anything; her Collapse is a tribute, not a specialty).
- [NEW v5-wk] **What the act is, in flavor (wk W01–W06):** Remnant extends an **appendage** that grabs the universe; its reach and intensity scale with Remnant, skill and focus (W01). The grip's acts, flavor-level only: shaking particles = heat; pulling charges apart = lightning; crushing or ripping the nucleus = explosions; turning a quark = transmutation, the hardest act (a botched one rips the nucleus); denting space = gravity (W02). [REV v5-cc] The dials are **Remnant, Will, Skill**; sense and touch sit inside Skill (cc R095); deeper work costs finer sense (W04); the grip is mechanized, and sensing is never explained on the page (W06); push past what the body holds and it burns out — the body breaks, never the Remnant (cc R096). (was: "Three dials — **Remnant** (strength), **control** (skill), **the inner sense** (an unexplained perception from Remnant, trainable and innate; e.g. the 'numb titan': huge Remnant, poor sense) (W03); deeper work costs finer sense — a gradient, not a gate (W04). 'You mostly feel with a second inner sense' — feel is a dial, not a gate (W05). The grip is mechanized; **the sense stays mysterious** — never explain it on the page (W06).")
- [NEW v5-wk] **Remnant is never burned or spent** (wk W10). Taking others' Remnant is "stealing their production" — [REV v5-wk2] [REV v5-cc] the mechanism is an amplifier — "I think its an amplifier only" (BANK 10-31); "drives their grip" retires (cc R132) (was: "the mechanism is 🌊 open — the thief driving their grip, or 'using an amplifier to touch a wider pool' (Patrick, chat t83: 'Im not sure')") (was: "the thief drives their grip" — Claude's t84 framing, never confirmed) (wk W11). Don't write souls or Remnant as fuel; where Patrick's existing drafts say "burns," a bracketed note flags it.

## Craft principle: the grimdark register 🟡 (locked this session — full detail in `09_STRUCTURE.md`)
The world is a brutal hellscape (betrayal, murder, slavery, abuse, fear, corruption) — and that brutality is a **forge**, not decoration: it manufactures the hardness that makes the showpieces parse (the master's indoctrinated self-sacrifice — formerly "the Strong-user's," label retired t136; Jon's coldness). Patrick's own label: "my work truly fits the label of grimdark" (t658). Hold these disciplines when writing:
- **Cost-and-characterize, never titillate.** Per scene: *does this reveal character or world, or is it just being watched?*
- **Contrast is the delivery system.** Tenderness is the *setup*; violence is the punchline [RESTORED v5-verify] (the kind moment before the loss is what makes the loss land). Unrelenting darkness goes numb — guard the ratio; the warmth must be real enough to hurt, not an obvious death-flag.
- **Simultaneity:** a small, funny, human moment running while a war kills millions offstage — sharpens both. The light lives in the protagonists (not everyone is cold, or there's nothing left to lose).
- **Nothing left to cheer for (t380):** "They all die. There can be nothing left to cheer for by the end when you watch Jon maybe choose to end everything." Everyone the reader loves dies in the Tower; no hopeful survivors. "In this world there's no room for redemption" (t354).
- **No corny goodness (t338):** a sympathetic monster stays a monster — the "good" changeling is still "in every way a murderous hungry user of other people"; only his demeanor changed.
- **An emotional blow, not a moral verdict (t558):** the ending's reveal doesn't forgive anyone — "Derrek is clearly a murderous tyrannical dictator. There's no real forgiveness. It's an emotional blow to the reader for the sake of compelling story."
- **What makes a killing land (t708):** "Everyone in this story has killed. A killing means little. It's the intensity and coldness of the killings. How useless the killing was. How cruel were their acts." Scale, intent, and the audience's feeling decide whether an act reads as unforgivable.
- [NEW v5-cc] **How gods fight (BANK 11-16 [HOW GODS FIGHT]):** "these are wizards. Big and tough doesnt mean throws punches" · "Try not to make it so slingy. Derrek just hurling fire balls. He is compressing matter ripping space sure but describe how that would look more than just he hurled ot at him." Show what the working looks like; no punch-ups, no thrown fireballs (cc R038).
- **Thesis the prose serves (t466):** "it doesn't matter in the grand scale but everything matters to someone."
- [NEW v5-wk] **Madness is subtext only (wk W70):** the base layer is the One dissociating, but no in-world metaphysical cause is ever visible on the page. It is nondiscriminate — "good and bad all are mad" (chat t365). [REV v5-wk2] (was: "and choice still carries the moral weight" — Claude's wording, chat t360/t366, never affirmed; Patrick at t361: "No you forget the one is subtext") Write behavior, never clinical labels (wk W44, W70; specific disorders per character are held).
- [NEW v5-jul] **Levity, dark jokes, more violence (jul08 t24):** "I want some levity and humor but they can be dark jokes and they can be punctuated by more violence." (The gnome changeling's "inappropriate jokes at the wrong moments," t762, is this rule in a character.)
- [NEW v5-jul] **An intervention is a plot point, not a rescue (jul23 t122–126):** a being far stronger than the hero may step in (e.g. a god who sees value in a challenger and wants to learn more or make a deal). That is "another expression of our system working as intended. A being making a choice for itself" (jul23 t124). "Its not the narrative saving a character. Its the narrative saving a character as a plot point" (jul23 t126). *(The god/angel/demon cast was reworked after this, t666–674; the craft rule stands either way.)*
- [NEW v5-jul] 🌊 **Tone direction, open:** Patrick: "I love Warhammer 40k and i dont think grimdark is enough... I dont want to just copy them of course but I would like to draw heavy inspiration" (jul23 t96, stated as "Think i have a tone change"); later he refers to "our grimdark 40k setting" (jul23 t154). Not ruled as a register law.

## Craft principle: the prose-cleaning rule 🟡 (t252–255)
**Production plan (t246–250, "maybe my best bet"):** Patrick writes the prose himself ("I have the skill for explaining and excitement and fun scenes"); Claude cleans it; a human editor/writer polishes.
**What "cleaning" means — mechanics only:** "cleaning means add syntax or grammar or punctuation. Make it easier to read. Not any actual story cleaning or word choice." So: punctuation, grammar, syntax, spelling, paragraph breaks. Words, sentences, and story stay untouched. No suggestions unless asked. Touch a word only where grammar strictly requires it (wrong tense, a missing "the"). Patrick: "That's what I need." *(Also belongs in `12_METHOD.md`.)*
- [REV v5-cc] **Claude drafts the prose from Patrick's ideas, through the story engine; Patrick's own lines are protected** (cc R106). Patrick, 2026-11-16: "One your writing my ideas. Same as always. Mostly do ignore anything gemini you or grok added and I didnt approve" (BANK 11-16 [PROCESS · prose and sources]); BANK 11-09 replaced t257 with Claude writing through the engine and Patrick adding his own lines where inspired. Anything an AI added that Patrick didn't approve is ignored. (was: "[NEW v5-wk2] **Every line of prose is Patrick's (chat t257):** *'Nah ive decided every line will be mine.'* Claude does not draft illustrative or scene prose; existing Claude-drafted passages in this file are record, not text to build on. (Rule → `12_METHOD.md`.)")
  - 🌊 *The production plan above (Patrick writes, Claude cleans, an editor polishes) and the cleaning rule are not re-ruled here; how they sit with engine drafting is for Patrick (L34).*

## [NEW v5-jul] Craft principle: drafting a scene 🟡 (jul08 t223–227; for Claude whenever it drafts or proposes scene text)
- **Dark, not a fairy tale.** "Your story reads like a kids fairy tale" (jul08 t223). A confrontation should be "intense accusations where you can feel the pain"; a dragon fight "needs to be menacing and a true battle not some silly wizard in the woods" (jul08 t223).
- **Traits without exposition.** "Each character and each scene ask yourself if you've fully expressed their traits without becoming blank exposition or weird ham fisted" (jul08 t223). No exposition dumps; reveals arrive suddenly, not telegraphed (jul08 t227).
- **Show it, don't state it.** Patrick's example: dwarves sell to everyone — "You dont have to tell the reader that tho. Just tell the reader there's a district in both cities as you explore them instead of stating it" (jul08 t225). *(The example was written for the old medieval Book 1 cities; the city layout itself belongs in `10_WORLD.md`.)*
- **But/therefore and real-world logic.** "Before you submit me incomplete or wrong scenes ask the but/therefore and also make sure it has some consistent logic with reality" (jul08 t225).
- **Stay inside the codex.** "Keep it to the codex so your not just inventing anything on the fly... be careful not to add details" (jul08 t223). One part at a time (jul08 t223). *(Process side — build the scene in chat before drafting, jul08 t237; core structure before surface detail, jul08 t245 — belongs in `12_METHOD.md`.)*

## Craft principle: POV & what the page shows 🟡
- **Final run only.** Only the final run is shown; earlier loops are implied residue, never dramatized. "We can have lines about 5k times before Jon. And the reader can see a glimpse of what they do" (t328). Earlier loops "literally never happened once he reset" (t330). *(v5-wk: the rule still holds; "the final run" is Jon's own lie — each run about 10,000 years, a thousand or more runs (wk W42). Book 1 shows no time travel (wk W53).)*
- **The war is off-screen; we watch a life.** "Jon and Derrek's war is mainly off screen... Derrek is hidden in his tower... Jon is off screen with the elves. So you're watching just the life of a hero living in the world they created until the pivotal moment" (t332).
- **The son is the reader's stand-in** — "and the reader can never hope to defeat the time god" (t372). The reader witnesses; the reader doesn't win.
- **The hero is a man, not a child.** "Boy" is the gods' view only — "Derrek and Jon are timeless; this guy could be 72 years old and he's a boy to them. It's not a child. He's a man" (t752). On the page he is capable, courageous, charming, "a man of equal resolve as either of the two gods" (t754); a powerful user who defeats dragons and giants with his crew and fights interdimensional monsters; the book is his rise and the Tower is "the final few chapters" (t756, t758).
- **Author-knowledge ≠ page-text.** "We don't have to write down in words Jon manipulated everything for it to be true" (t402). The author knows; the page need not say it.
- **Writing Jon (the iceberg).** He **SAYS charming things and DOES selfish, cruel things** (t746, t748). On the page readers "see him feel a lot. He's very charismatic or else he wouldn't be likeable. Only we know he doesn't feel anything" (t744). Signature staging: "him comforting the boy as he casually does something brutal" (t748) — the **same-moment** technique: hand on the shoulder, kind voice, the other hand finishing something terrible, eyes on the hero's face, no tonal shift (t749).
  - [NEW v5-wk] **The true villain, written sincere (wk W44, W49):** Jon is warm, honest, sincere — Bondrewd-like — openly sincere, **not** hiding behind a savior image; only the Lirael secret is hidden. Book 1 Jon reads as eccentric and charming; in his true form he is cold during the Tower ascent; the context comes in Jon's own book.
- [NEW v5-wk] **Soul-sensing on the page (wk W07, W09):** sensing another being's Remnant is a rare master-level skill; the elven bond is innate and collective but does **not** track individuals — an elf who dies far away dies alone, without the bond (wk W08). On the page it must be rare, felt rather than reported, and unreliable — never "video gamey," no constant scanning or detecting. [v5-verify-wk: 🌊 "felt rather than reported" and "unreliable" are Claude's specifics (chat t226), unconfirmed; rarity and anti-"video gamey" are Patrick's (t223, t225) — L35.]
- **Everyone learns Jon's truth at the very end — including Jon "in a sense" — except Derrek, who always knew** (t556).
- [NEW v5-wk2] 🟡 **Writing the son and the queen as pawns (chat t201):** the son has no will and no name — *"the son has no name because he was never meant to be named. His name will come last."* Don't build his wants up front; his hopes live only in scenes and slowly fade. The queen is likewise a nameless pawn who sacrifices herself for Jon.
- 🌊 Whether the hero is the single POV protagonist throughout is not ruled (Claude's framing, t703).

## PART TWO — THE GIANTS' AGE (visual register & the canon duel)

## Visual register: the Giants' Age 🟡 (t22–30, t32–34, t60–62, t88, t292, t300)
- **Dark Souls is the visual key — for the world design, not the comparison** ("the point wasn't the comparison, it was the world design," t22–29). Monument-scale giant architecture, used by beings as large as Dark Souls bosses; **every later power occupies it** (dragons, then humans).
- **Grown, not built.** Giant architecture is grown/willed and **seamless — no chisel marks**; giants understand complex chain bonds well enough to make compounds that let their size stand forever (t29–30). The far-future cathedral ships are the same craft.
- **The dead are in the walls — as power, not as residents.** [REV v5-wk] (was: "The mason fuels the build with a dead giant's Remnant") The mason grows the build with a dead giant's Remnant — Remnant is never burned or spent (wk W10), and matter can hold a soul (wk W12); how the walls relate to that Remnant is for Patrick (CONFLICTS): "You aren't now the walls of a castle; your power was the source used to grow the walls themselves" (t34). Image to keep: dragons "physically sitting inside the remains of the giant family who built those halls" (t32).
- **Too big for the people who came after.** Dragon palaces are giant-built buildings "too large for humanity to ever have really moved into. Just impossible to climb, some, in any reasonable way" (t300).
- **The Tower** is the giants' grandest crown gem (t60) — in truth the converged giant king (t87) — a "giant pearly tower sticking into the clouds" (t292). Derrek built **additions only**: "elevators and laser arrays and teleprompter rooms, not the walls itself" (t62). The blast region was radioactive for a long time — another reason animals avoid it and it carries weird legend (t88). *(v5-wk: the emperor's Convergence used the city's bodies as material and trapped the city's Remnant in the stone; he was a mix of souls and dissolved; the Tower is the largest giant city, compressed — wk W15–W16; [REV v5-cc] mindless, cc R111 (was: "still faintly feeling").)*
- 🌊 Not yet in sources (do not write as canon until Patrick confirms): "scale as melancholy," "wrong myths over right ruins."

## Showpiece seed: the canon duel — the giant king converges into the Tower 🟡 (Patrick's beats, t82–90; revised t262–268, t408, t440)
**Frame (as revised):** the opening day of the dragons' betrayal, in the heart of the giant capital. The dragon is **not** the ruler of dragons — he is the **closest advisor to the giant emperor**, "called the king in memory by those he sacrificed himself to set on the thrones. He was never the ruler of dragons and he resented it" (t268). So the duel is betrayal by the most trusted friend at court. **He knew what he was doing:** "He was such a capable user and he knew what he created. It was his life's work. He knew from his testing of other ones this was the end... he decided that meant sacrificing himself to destroy the heart of giant power to free his people" (t262). The capital's dragons (courtiers, envoys, guards, family) stayed and burned as camouflage — "acceptable losses in his calculations" (t264). He had mastered transmutation and the blast "in a time before they understood the principles" (t440); the stone was "a medieval form of his fissile material" (t408).
**Beats (Patrick, t82–86):**
1. The giant "lays a pure em field around himself capable of deflecting all forms of matter. They literally disintegrate into harmless elements and drift off as a mist as they land." He begins his gravity attack — he has "centered the dragon with the singularity and the world is bending around the dragon." [REV v5-xfile] (was: 'lays a field around himself "capable of…' — Patrick's own words restored, t82; the page-rule below still applies at drafting.)
2. The dragon recognizes the field, has "seen this before," and goes to his ultimate move: "He spits out a chunk of special rock he synthesized with weak force and saved within a cavity in his stomach. He bites it between his teeth and uses all his focus to shatter it. The moment it breaks he concentrates maximum Remnant output." [REV v5-xfile] (was: "synthesized... and saved" — the ellipsis dropped Patrick's "with weak force," t82.) (The rock is how the move stays rare: "He used his trump card; if it fails that's it unless he prepared more," t84.)

The giant "slowly loses himself to its warm embrace. He pours the last of his energy into fully becoming a giant stone tower" — and the dragon is consumed in radioactive fire as he violently explodes with his last attack. The capital goes with them.

**On the page:** per the scaffolding rule, describe the acts and sensations; never label "EM," "gravity," or "strong force" in narration (Patrick's beat names them as our shorthand).

## Showpiece: the dragon godfather and the gnome changeling 🟡 (Patrick's scene, t282–296; t336–338, t772)
The same morning. The advisor passes "one of the other advisors he always liked. A small old gnome. No one ever understood how this gnome managed to gain the giant emperor's ear." The dragon "had sniffed out he was a changeling at some point through a series of interrogational questions" and chose to support him. The reader has always known the gnome is a changeling and assumes it's over — instead the dragon warns him in the cryptic way we come to know: **"you may like visiting home today — nice warm sunny weather for a quick horse ride out of the city."**
- **Why only the dragon saw:** "everyone else is so self-centered and self-important they never spend long enough to actually question what they have seen the gnome capable of. Not the dragon. He sees everything" (t286).
- **Why he spares him:** the eternal-messenger motive — he thinks changelings are "smaller beings," the one being who could never truly rival him ("or so he thought — a sufficiently powerful changeling can absolutely possess a dragon"), "so he sends the eternal man off to spin his tales" (t288).
- **The ride:** the gnome "took it very serious"; the dragon "was the only being who ever looked at him and truly saw him"; he didn't flee knowing it was a nuke — he "was terrified because his cover was blown by the one being there he was terrified of" (t290). He is barely off the edge of the blast and **fine** — "he had time" (t292).
- **The look back — order matters (t294):** "The first thing he sees is absolute devastation. Complete ruin. A giant billowing mushroom cloud of pure death and fire as far as he can see. THEN out of the ruin he sees the tower emerge" — "a crater larger than anything he's ever seen... the giant pearly tower sticking into the clouds" (t292). Patrick: the reader sees both happen at once so it isn't confusing (t296).
- **What it sets in motion:** the first time he felt respected "for who he is, not who he was pretending to be" — the start of the long chain that makes him the far future's "good" changeling (t336), calibrated per t338 (see grimdark). He is **a gnome who became a changeling**, a consumer *(changeling sense — not the fractal-level "consumer" title, wk W36)* who loves his gnomish body and only occasionally moves into a similar gnome body when he has to (t772). [REV v5-jul] (was: "so in this scene he is wearing his own face" — an inference; whether the court gnome is his first body is not stated.) *(v5-wk 🟡 clay: he is also the gnome god — wk W23, W33; an ascended changeling is not a "god" in the singular sense — wk W32.)*

[RESTORED v5-verify] *(Full -4 wording of the device, kept for the refit; the detonation/inferno lines are retired below:)* Light is energy, so nothing inside can reach the friends' eyes — **the seeing is the BEAST'S cruelty.** The Rule is its own construct; it authored a spectator clause: **the domain renders its interior on its outer face** (the beast perceives its domain natively and *displays* it, paid in its own coherence — no interior energy ever crosses, so "nothing, including energy, leaves" stays literally true). The irony completes: the window it opened to savor their grief instead frames the goodbye, then broadcasts the first instant of its own eternity. **The reader, however, is in both rooms:** show the silent helpless watching from outside *and* describe the full interior reality the friends can't perceive — the agony, the forces, everything they're missing — at once. (Microcosm of the whole series: the present witnesses see only the surface; the truth is given to the reader.)
**The gravity rhyme (t434):** this is the first gravity death in the Tower, and it **works** — "We see gravity succeed first, then we think the 2nd time like they messed up that beast with that attack! Then watch as she does not survive" (see the bishop, below).

## Showpiece: the queen vs. the apprentice 🟡 (Patrick's scene, t764–768)
**The queen** — Jon's hand-selected champion and the hero's **rival** ("The elf to the hero's human. **Patrick's sequence (t768):** the apprentice, tears in his eyes, pushes past his limit, lets Remnant surge through him, spends everything to protect his god and prove his worth. His technique (placeholder name: "Soul infused leftover mana recycling discharge") is one "he developed when he began sensing the latent pools of Remnant in this tower" — he draws Remnant from the rifts into his body, begins to shine, weapon charged with light, "absolute tolerance against melee attacks," and charges in a blinding burst. The queen is caught off guard by the speed and defends; "two martial operators use Remnant for maximum enhancement." ## PART FIVE — OTHER SHOWPIECES (kept)

## Showpiece: the entropy-breath god-killer 🌊 (far-future set-piece)
**The mechanism (per the aging law, Constitution 4a):** even a god is *flesh that ages* — so **entropy/death magic** doesn't out-muscle the god (impossible), it **accelerates the dissolution/aging even a god's flesh can't escape.** More Remnant = more resistance = succumbs *later*, **never immune.** That gradient IS the scene's structure.
**The scene:** an enemy "god" **teleports onto a dragon's immaculate giant-built starship** — crewed by humans, elves, dwarves, orcs (a representation of the whole planet), the dragon on his throne, the crew at their stations **behind the god.** The dragon — who does **NOT care about his crew at all** (cold race-characterization; they're expendable, not a heartbeat's hesitation) — **fires preemptively**, unleashing his **secret entropy breath** straight through the god (and through his own crew behind him). *The dragon is the CASTER, never a casualty — do not invent dragon-peril.*
**The escalation (the gradient made visible):** the breath "doesn't seem to do much at first." Then the [RESTORED v5-verify] dragon's crew behind the god begin to **age/dissolve toward maximum entropy — in ASCENDING order of Remnant/lifespan:** the **orc bursts first** (least resistance), then **humans**, then **dwarves**, then **elves** — each death buying a beat, the horror **climbing the ladder.** The **god stands unmoving**, cocky, certain he's beyond it — *boasts* ("your crew is dead, how will you get home?"). The **dragon sweats with doubt** [RESTORED v5-verify] (his secret technique seems to have failed). Then the god — most resistant, having **never felt a bodily sensation** in his existence — **trembles, confused**, and **begins to age/dissolve LAST.** [RESTORED v5-verify] Dawning horror: he was never *exempt*, only *delayed* — his resistance bought him a front-row seat to his own doom [RESTORED v5-verify] (he watched the ladder climb toward him). The being who believed himself beyond flesh learns he was always flesh.
**Why it lands:** the god and the orc die the *same death*, separated only by Remnant — the duality and the aging law fused [RESTORED v5-verify] (greatest and lowliest, the same kind of thing, taken in order by the only thing that ever differed). *(Entropy magic is rare/terrible — a dragon's secret breath [RESTORED v5-verify] — high on the difficulty scale; science-FLAVOR only, NO homework on "how it forces maximum entropy.")*

## Duel draft: deep Water/little Earth vs. Fire/Air (EM) 🌊
Used to test "levels invisible on the page." The cornered fighter (deep, patient, lethal up close) survives the aggressor's cheap relentless burst by **outlasting the burn with efficiency**, turns his **corrosive fog into a fluid she seizes**, collapses it to tip him toward her, then kills by **reversing the pressure of the blood in his chest** (precise internal lethality). His fast opening *should* win; her efficiency + intimate kill win if she survives it. Two versions drafted in-session; the second fully dissolves all level-language into sensation. *(Originally written with force/element-cluster labels, now RETIRED — there are no clusters and no "types." Re-read for the **acts and sensations** only [RESTORED v5-verify]: describe what each fighter does and how it feels; name the flavor loosely after, never assign either a "type.")*
